sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: Which three functions do road markings serve, and which three paint colors carry them?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Road markings guide, warn, and regulate traffic in red, yellow, or white, used alone or combined.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: Where might you spot red paint, and who sees red pavement reflectors glowing ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Red markings are rare, though some towns use red curbs for no parking; red pavement reflectors face wrong-way traffic only.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: What traffic flow do yellow center lines indicate, and what does a single broken yellow line permit?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Yellow center lines mean two-way opposite-direction traffic, and a broken yellow center allows passing on the left in either direction when ahead is clear.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Where a broken yellow stripe runs beside a solid yellow stripe, who can pass cars and when can the solid side cross?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line allows passing only from the broken side; solid-side drivers may cross only for pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter and skateboard riders when the opposite lane is clear and safe.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: What passing rule do double solid yellow lines set, and what two exceptions allow crossing them?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Double solid yellow lines mark the road center between opposing flows: no passing either way, crossing only for left turns or for pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter and skateboard riders when the opposite lane is clear and safe.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: How do passing rights change between a broken-plus-solid yellow centerline and double solid yellow lines?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Broken-plus-solid yellow lets the broken side pass, while double solid yellow lets neither side pass.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: When a solid yellow stripe sits on your side, which road users may you cross it to pass?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: From the solid-yellow side you may cross only for pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter and skateboard riders with the far lane clear.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: When is passing a slower vehicle on the left legal along an unmarked two-lane Virginia road?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: On an unmarked two-lane road, you may pass a slow vehicle on the left where no signs prohibit passing and the way is clear.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: Which lanes do broken white lines separate, and how should you treat crossing them?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Broken white lines divide same-direction lanes: change lanes with caution.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: What core difference separates a broken yellow line from a broken white line?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Broken yellow divides opposing directions with passing allowed, while broken white divides same-direction lanes with changes allowed.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: Where does Virginia paint short dotted white lines, and how do they help drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Dotted white lines assign lanes through intersections and interchanges, guide paired turning lanes, and mark turn-lane openings and entrance and exit lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How does the job of standard broken white dashes differ from short dotted white lines?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Broken white opens free lane changes, while dotted white steers lanes through intersections and ramps.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: What lane boundaries and fixed features use solid white markings on Virginia roads?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: Solid white lines mark turn lanes and the right pavement edge, discourage changes near intersections and ramps, and pair with arrows that dictate the allowed turn; stop lines, crosswalks, and parking spaces also use white.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: What does a row of white triangles painted across your lane indicate?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: A yield line of triangles across the road, often with a yield sign or at a roundabout entrance, marks where to yield or stop.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: How does a triangle yield line contrast with solid white stop bars, crosswalks, and parking lines?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: Yield triangles mark a yield-or-stop point, while white stop lines, crosswalks, and parking marks fix exact positions.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: How do your movement options change between a solo curved pavement arrow and a combined curved-and-straight arrow?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: A curved arrow alone or with ONLY means you must turn that way, while a curved plus straight arrow means you may turn or go straight.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: Which pavement arrow locks you into turning, and which gives you the choice to continue straight?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: A curved arrow alone or with ONLY forces the turn, while a curved plus straight arrow offers turn or straight.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: What emergency do wrong-way pavement arrows signal, and what immediate action must you take?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Wrong-way arrows mean you are driving against traffic toward a head-on crash: slow down and pull over at once.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: What rule governs double solid white lines separating same-direction lanes such as HOV corridors?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Double solid white lines divide same-direction lanes, often shielding special-use lanes like HOV lanes: never cross them, entering only where signs and markings allow.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: On a three-lane two-way road, which two maneuvers can a marked center lane serve?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: On three-lane two-way roads, the marked center lane serves left turns or passing.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: What does a center lane bordered by single broken yellow stripes on both sides allow?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: A center lane with a broken yellow line on both sides is open to passing from either direction.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: What is a center lane edged by solid outer and broken inner yellow stripes for, and what travel limit applies?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: A center lane with solid plus broken yellow on both sides is open to left turns from either direction, but never to more than one hundred fifty feet of travel.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: How do three-lane center markings distinguish a shared passing lane from a shared left-turn lane?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: A center lane broken on both sides allows passing from either way, while a center lane solid-plus-broken allows only left turns within one hundred fifty feet.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: What road setup does a sharrow mark, and what should motorists anticipate there?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: A sharrow pairs a bicycle symbol with a double chevron on lanes too narrow to share side by side: bicyclists ride there and drivers expect them.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: How are preferential bicycle lanes marked, and under what sole condition may motorists enter one?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: Bicycle lanes marked by solid or dashed white lines or green pavement with a bike symbol stay preferential for bikes; drivers enter only to turn, after mirror checks and yielding to lane bikes.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: How does sharing space over a sharrow differ from driving alongside a dedicated bicycle lane?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: A sharrow shares a narrow lane with bikes riding in it, while a bike lane reserves its space with entry only for turns.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: Which four rules apply to motorists at an intersection painted with a bicycle box?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: Bicycle boxes at intersections hold waiting riders ahead of drivers: stop behind the box on red, never inside it, make no right on red there, and on green signal right turns while yielding to bikes on the right.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: Which two pavement cues identify a lane restricted exclusively to buses?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: Bus-only lanes carry BUS ONLY markings, red-colored pavement, or both.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: How are HOV lanes marked and separated, who qualifies during restricted hours, and how do barrier lanes operate?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: HOV lanes carry center diamonds and may run barrier-separated or behind double white lines; in heavy traffic they serve buses, vanpools, carpools, high-occupancy vehicles, motorcycles, and certain clean-fuel vehicles, with signs posting minimum passengers and hours, and barrier lanes reverse direction by time of day.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: Besides high-occupancy carpool corridors, what other restricted travel lane can a painted diamond designate?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: A diamond marking can also reserve a lane for buses.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: How does driver eligibility differ between diamond-marked HOV lanes and red bus-only lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: Center diamonds open HOV lanes to qualified high-occupancy travel, while BUS ONLY paint and red pavement close bus lanes to all but buses.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: What three hazard categories do portable and overhead message boards report, and how must you treat them?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Portable and permanent message boards report traffic, road, and weather hazards: always obey their directions.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: How should you steer and manage speed when rumble strip warnings appear ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: Rumble strip warnings mean driving slowly straight over the strips, never swerving around them.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: How does your response to an electronic message board compare with crossing transverse rumble strips?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: Message boards issue directions to obey, while rumble strips issue a surface to cross slowly and straight.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: What speed ceiling and vehicle types carry slow-moving vehicle signs, and how must you react?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Slow moving vehicles at twenty-five miles per hour or less, such as farm equipment, horse-drawn vehicles, and work vehicles, display warning signs; adjust your speed or position for them.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: Which transponder works statewide at Virginia tolls, how do purple-logo and cash lanes split, and what hazards lurk?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: Every Virginia toll facility accepts E-ZPass transponders: follow purple-logo lanes with one, cash lanes without one, slowing with caution for lane changers and crossing employees.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: Why must you never stop or back up if you enter a high-speed E-ZPass lane without a transponder?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: High-speed E-ZPass lanes are transponder-only; a mistaken entry must never stop, since cameras photograph the plate and bill the registered owner.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: How do purple-logo booths, cash lanes, and high-speed transponder chutes each handle drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.memory_hook: Purple tags, cash pays, express rolls
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: Purple-logo lanes serve transponder holders and cash lanes serve the rest, while high-speed transponder lanes punish a mistaken entry with no stopping.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: After checking local ordinances, what curbside rules usually pair with white, yellow, and red paint?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.memory_hook: White passengers, yellow loading, red zero
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: Painted curbs set parking rules to confirm with the locality: white allows only passenger pickup and dropoff, yellow allows only loading with the driver staying, and red bans stopping, standing, and parking.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.front: Which painted curb lets passengers hop in, which requires staying with cargo, and which forbids stopping?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.memory_hook: White dropoff, yellow stay, red none
sec05-card-sec05-R12.expected_back: White curbs serve passenger pickup and dropoff, yellow curbs serve loading with the driver present, and red curbs ban stopping, standing, and parking.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: Which lane starts and finishes a right turn, how early do you signal, and what scanning and braking rules apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Turn right from the lane furthest right: signal three or four seconds, one hundred feet, ahead, look left and right for pedestrians and traffic, brake before and during, stop fully at red lights and stop signs, and enter the lane closest to the curb unless markings lead otherwise.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: From which lane into which lane do you turn left, how should your front wheels point while waiting, and whom do you yield to?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: Turn left from the furthest left lane into the leftmost lane unless markings or multiple turn lanes direct otherwise: signal three or four seconds, one hundred feet, ahead, look all ways including opposite traffic, hold wheels straight until committed, and yield to opposite vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: Contrast the starting and ending lane rules for a standard right turn versus a standard left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: Right turns start furthest right and end curb-side, while left turns start furthest left and end leftmost.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: When two opposing vehicles both signal left turns at an intersection, how should they pass each other?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Two opposing vehicles signaling left turns pass in front of each other with their passenger sides beside each other.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: Which two signs must you look for before a U-turn, where are town or business U-turns restricted, and what about highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Before any U-turn, check for No U-Turn or No Left Turn signs; in business districts, cities, and towns U-turns are allowed only at intersections, and never on a highway.
pills: NO U OR NO LEFT SIGN

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: How many of the three U-turn checks — prohibitive signs, mid-block town streets, or highways — does it take to make a U-turn illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: U-turns need clear signs, town intersections, and no highway; each condition bans them alone.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: Walk through the four signal, stop, yield, and target-lane steps for making a U-turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: To U-turn, signal left, stop, yield to approaching traffic, and when clear enter the outside or right-hand lane of the opposite direction.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: How does a U-turn's stopping and target-lane rule differ from a normal left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: U-turns add a full stop and yield before entering the far lane, while left turns yield without stopping.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: Which maneuvers legally require turn or hand signals, must you signal on an empty street, and what follows the move?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Turn signals are required by law for lane changes, turns, and highway entries and exits; use them or hand signals even with no traffic around, and cancel the signal after finishing.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: How many seconds and feet before a turn should you signal — and what mistake by side-street drivers should you watch for?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Signal three or four seconds, one hundred feet, before your turn, and stay alert for drivers who may pull out misjudging where you will turn.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: When does your turn signal go on before a maneuver, and what must happen once you finish?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Signals open three to four seconds ahead of the move and must be canceled after it.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: Using your left arm out the window, which positions signal a left turn, a right turn, and slowing or stopping?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Hand signals use the left arm: straight out for a left turn, pointing up for a right turn, and pointing down for slowing or stopping.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: Match each left-arm position — straight out, bent upward, and bent downward — to its driving meaning?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Left arm straight means left, left arm up means right, and left arm down means slow or stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: What does steering over-correction do to your rear wheels, how should you enter curves, and how do you recover if you veer off?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Over-correcting steers more sharply than expected and slides the rear wheels outward, risking control loss; slow down on curves, and if you veer off, ease off speed without panic, look where you want to go, and steer back slowly.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: What steering mistake slides the rear wheels outward, and what three calm habits bring you safely back on track?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Over-correction slides the rear out from sharp steering, and recovery means easing speed, aiming eyes, and steering back slowly.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: Where do you position inside your lane and keep open buffers to build a protective space cushion?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Build a space cushion by centering your lane and keeping room ahead and behind so vehicles can pass or stop safely.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: On dry pavement, how many following seconds match under thirty-five, thirty-five to forty-five, and forty-six to seventy — and above seventy?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: On dry roads follow at two seconds under thirty-five miles per hour, three seconds from thirty-five to forty-five, and four seconds from forty-six to seventy; the rule fails above seventy.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: Pair each Virginia following-distance count — two, three, four, and none — with its exact speed bracket?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Two seconds serve under thirty-five, three serve thirty-five to forty-five, four serve forty-six to seventy, and none serve above seventy.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: How do you measure your following seconds with a fixed roadside object, and which four conditions call for extra seconds?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Time your gap from a fixed object the car ahead passes: arriving early means too close, so slow and widen; add seconds for bad weather, heavy traffic, poor pavement, or a poor vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: Roughly how fast do hands versus feet react — and which human and vehicle factors stretch perception and stopping?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Hand response runs near a half second and foot response near three-quarters, before perception delays from tiredness, medication, or distraction; conditions, speed, alertness, and vehicle weight all change stopping.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: How does average hand reaction time compare with average foot reaction time before impairment delays even start?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Hands answer in about a half second and feet in about three-quarters, before tiredness, medication, or distraction add more.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Behind which vehicles and in which road or traffic situations must you stretch your normal following gap?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Widen following distance behind vision-blocking large vehicles, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting expressways, behind motorcycles or bicycles, and when being tailgated.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: How does counting past a fixed landmark work alongside knowing when to add extra seconds?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: Fixed-object timing detects a short gap, while large vehicles, weather, exits, small bikes, and tailgaters demand a longer one.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: What brake mistake must you avoid when tailgated, how do you shake a tailgater, and how do you help normal followers?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: When tailgated, never brake suddenly: move over or tap the brakes to flash and slow; help followers with a steady speed and brake taps before slowing or stopping.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Contrast your response to an aggressive tailgater with everyday courteous driving for cars behind you?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: The tailgated driver moves over or flashes brakes to slow, while the considerate driver holds steady speed with early brake taps.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: How many seconds — or city blocks — ahead should you aim your focus, and how should your eyes work the scene?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Search the whole scene with moving eyes, focus twenty to thirty seconds ahead or about one city block, and scan side to side for signs, signals, cars, and people.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: Which parked-car clues warn someone is pulling out — and what extra hazards appear on rural roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Read road clues like exhaust smoke, brake or backup lights, and turned wheels; watch for pedestrians, bicyclists, and slow vehicles, and in rural areas for hidden junctions, curves, hills, trucks, and farm equipment.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: Which scan order checks an intersection — and why that side first — plus how often and when do you check mirrors?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Enter intersections with a left-right-left look, left first as the nearer threat; check the rearview about every ten seconds and before lane changes, backing, quick slows, and long descents.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: Put Virginia's three scanning habits together — forward focus seconds, rearview mirror interval, and intersection head scan?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: Eyes run twenty to thirty seconds ahead, mirrors check about every ten seconds, and intersections get left-right-left.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: How should you aim your inside and side mirrors, and what physical check clears blind spots before lane changes or passes?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Set the inside mirror to frame the whole back window and the side mirrors to barely show your vehicle; clear blind spots with a quick head turn and shoulder glance before lane changes and passes.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: What two speed adjustments keep you from lingering inside another driver's blind spot?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Never linger in another driver's blind spot: speed up or drop back instead.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: Contrast how you manage your own vehicle's blind spots with how you handle another driver's blind spots?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: Your own blind spots need mirror setup plus head checks, while others' blind spots need you to speed up or drop back out.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Who counts as a vulnerable road user in Virginia, what driving conduct around them is illegal, and what duty applies?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Vulnerable users cover pedestrians, bicyclists, wheelchair, skateboard, skate, and scooter users, animals, and animal-drawn vehicles; distracted or careless driving around them is illegal, and you must drive to cover their mistakes.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: Where must you stay extra alert for walkers, and what turning, passing, and lane-clearing rules protect crosswalks?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: Guard pedestrians near schools, playgrounds, and homes; let them fully cross before you turn; never pass at a crosswalk; stop and stay stopped until they clear your stopped lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: For whom must Virginia drivers come to a full stop, and what criminal charge hits failing to stop and causing serious injury or death?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Come to a full stop for cane or guide-dog users and for any pedestrian lawfully crossing; failing to stop and causing serious injury or death brings a Class one misdemeanor.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How does waiting out a crossing while turning pair with Virginia's full-stop rule and serious-injury penalty?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Turning drivers wait out full crossings, while cane, guide-dog, and lawful crossings demand full stops backed by a Class one misdemeanor.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: Where may bicyclists ride on Virginia roads and lanes, which highways bar them, and where may they approach from either direction?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Bicyclists share motor-vehicle right-of-way, may hold the lane center when needed for left turns or narrow lanes, ride all public roads except interstates and most freeways, and may approach from either direction on sidewalks, paths, and two-way bike lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: How much side clearance must you give when passing a bicyclist, when must you change lanes, and may cars enter marked bike lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Pass cyclists with at least three feet of clearance, changing lanes where the lane cannot spare it; motor vehicles may never use marked bike lanes, even to pass.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: Balance what Virginia grants bicyclists on the road against the three space rules owed by drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Bicyclists may take the lane center and most roads, while drivers owe them three feet, lane changes, and empty bike lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: At which six everyday driving or parking moments must you scan specifically for bicycles — and what bike move should you expect?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: Bicycles slip easily into blind spots: check for them before pull-outs, lane changes, turns, backing, door openings, and intersections, give room, and expect sudden stops.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: In what share of car-motorcycle crashes did the car driver miss seeing the bike in time — and why does that happen?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: Look twice for motorcycles, since drivers expect four-wheelers and miss bikes until too late in over half of car-motorcycle crashes; check blind spots before every maneuver.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: Pair why bicycles need checks at six maneuver points with why motorcycles demand double looks?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: Bikes need checks at six maneuver points for their slipperiness, while motorcycles need double looks for their invisibility.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: What lane-sharing, dry following-time, wet following-time, and swerve rules apply behind a motorcycle?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: Never tailgate or lane-share with a motorcycle: add an extra second of following distance, double it in bad weather, expect sudden in-lane moves, and yield with double looks since bike speed and distance deceive.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: Summarize the four space and time protections Virginia gives a motorcyclist ahead of your car?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: Motorcycles gain an extra following second doubled in weather, plus bans on tailgating and lane sharing.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: How many crossings span Norfolk's seven-point-four-mile light rail The Tide, and what gate, track, and turning rules apply?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Around Norfolk light rail The Tide, with twenty-seven crossings over seven point four miles, expect trains on any track at any time, never circle lowered gates or stop, pass, or shift on tracks, look both ways before turning across, and cross only with room to clear fully.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: Separate what light-rail crossings strictly forbid from the three habits they require?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: Light rail forbids circling gates and stopping on tracks, while demanding train expectation, double looks, and full clearance.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: What top-speed band defines low-speed vehicles, which roads and drivers may run them, and do golf carts qualify?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: Low-speed vehicles top out at twenty-one to twenty-five miles per hour and may run only on roads posted thirty-five miles per hour or less for licensed drivers or supervised permit holders, meeting federal safety plus Virginia registration and insurance rules; golf carts do not qualify.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: Contrast a street-legal Virginia low-speed vehicle's speed and road limit against a golf cart?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Low-speed vehicles run twenty-one to twenty-five on roads of thirty-five or less, while golf carts are not low-speed vehicles at all.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: How do trucks, tractor-trailers, buses, and RVs handle compared with cars, and where sit their No-Zones?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Trucks, tractor-trailers, buses, and RVs run longer, higher, and wider with slow acceleration and long stopping and turning needs; their danger areas are called No-Zones on the sides, front, and rear.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: Why are side No-Zones so dangerous on trucks, buses, and RVs — and what mirror rule tells whether the driver sees you?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Side No-Zones on trucks, buses, and RVs dwarf car blind spots because of wide turns: if you cannot see the driver's face in his mirror, he cannot see you.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: What two sight losses and crash trap hit drivers who tailgate inside a truck's rear No-Zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Rear No-Zones hide your car from the truck driver and hide ahead traffic from you, leaving no escape at sudden stops; always hold a safe following distance.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: Why do front No-Zones punish cutting in early — including truck stopping ratio, sixty-five-foot length, half-mile pass, and mirror cue?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Front No-Zones punish cutting in too soon or slowing after passing, since trucks need nearly twice car stopping time and room; combinations run up to sixty-five feet and may need over half a mile to pass, so return only with the whole truck front in your mirror and hold speed.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: Match the side, rear, and front truck No-Zones to the specific crash hazard each creates?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: Side zones hide you beside wide-turning trucks, rear zones hide you behind sudden stoppers, and front zones punish early cut-ins.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: How far ahead and behind can large-vehicle blind spots reach, and what must you never do beside a turning rig?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: Trucks, buses, and RVs swing wide to turn with blind spots up to twenty feet ahead of the cab and about two hundred feet behind; never squeeze between them and the curb or another vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: Contrast safe positioning when merging ahead of an overtaken truck versus approaching a turning truck?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: Passing returns need the whole truck front in the mirror at steady speed, while turning trucks forbid squeezing past at all.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: What hitching and mirror gear do light or medium trailers need, and how much does towing multiply driving effort?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Light and medium trailers ride on safety chains and hitches with large mirrors needed; towing doubles passing, stopping, accelerating, and turning effort, and No-Zones apply.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: How does towing a trailer compare with a large truck's stopping demand?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: Trailers double every maneuver's effort, matching trucks' near-double stopping demand.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: What mistake causes most backing crashes, and what posture and speed should you use when reversing?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.memory_hook: Turn right, look back, reverse slowly
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Drivers backing up most often fail to look both ways behind; mirrors leave gaps, so twist body and head right to sight through the rear window, reverse slowly, and flick glances to each side for walkers and traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: Which three groups of road users must you check for before opening a parked car door?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.memory_hook: Scan cars, cyclists, and walkers first
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Before swinging a door open, scan for cars, bicyclists, and pedestrians around the parked vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How does the visual check required to reverse a car differ from the check before stepping out?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.memory_hook: Twist to reverse, scan before exiting
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: Backing needs a body twist to the rear window with slow reversing, while exiting only needs a scan for cars, bikes, and walkers before the door swings.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: How close to a curb should you park, and which road sides are legal on two-way versus one-way streets?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.memory_hook: Within one foot, right on two-way
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Park as far from traffic as the road allows: deep onto shoulders, tight to curbs within one foot, on the right of two-way streets, and on either side of one-way roads.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: How do legal parking sides compare between a two-way street and a one-way roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: Two-way streets park right only, while one-way roads park either side.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: When parking on a hill with a curb, which way do you turn your front wheels uphill versus downhill?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: Where a curb exists on a hill, set the front wheels to block a streetward roll: aim them left when parked facing uphill and right when parked facing downhill.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: When parking uphill or downhill where there is no curb, which direction must your front wheels point?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.memory_hook: No curb always turns wheels right
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Without a curb on a hill, point the front wheels right so any roll sends the rear away from traffic, whether facing uphill or downhill.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: How does curb parking on level pavement differ from curb parking on a hill?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.memory_hook: Flat within foot, hills angle wheels
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Curb parking hugs within one foot on the flat, while hill parking with a curb angles wheels left uphill and right downhill.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: How does wheel direction on a curbed hill differ from wheel direction on an uncurbed hill?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.memory_hook: Curbs split direction, uncurbed stays right
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Hills with a curb split wheel direction by grade, left up and right down, while hills without a curb always point wheels right.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: Which roadway spots, markings, and lanes are off-limits for parking even without measuring footage?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.memory_hook: Never double-park or block travel spaces
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Parking is banned beside another parked vehicle, on crosswalks and sidewalks, ahead of driveways, at yellow curbs and No Parking signs, in disabled spaces and their striped aisles, on hard road surface where no curb runs, in bike lanes, and anywhere the car blocks or endangers a traffic lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: What minimum footage must you leave around hydrants, rescue entrances, intersections, railroad crossings, and active fire trucks?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.memory_hook: Fifteen hydrant, twenty corner, fifty rail
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Keep clear within fifteen feet of hydrants, within twenty feet of intersections, within fifteen feet of fire, ambulance, or rescue station entrances, within five hundred feet of fire equipment working an alarm, and within fifty feet of railroad crossings.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: How do Virginia's location-based parking bans differ from its footage-based clearance rules?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.memory_hook: Banned zones versus measured buffer feet
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: Some bans name places like crosswalks and driveways, while others name distances like fifteen hydrant feet and twenty intersection feet.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: What root failure causes most crashes, and what scanning and lighting habits guard against it?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.memory_hook: Scan every direction, burn lights early
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: Crashes trace most to missed risks: keep track of surrounding vehicles, scan ahead, to the sides, and behind, stay ready for walkers and cyclists, and switch headlights on at night and in poor sight.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: Under Virginia law, what visibility distance and windshield-wiper rule trigger mandatory headlights in bad weather?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.memory_hook: Five hundred feet or wipers running
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: State law demands headlights in rain, fog, snow, or sleet once sight drops to five hundred feet, and whenever wipers run for bad weather; burning them even by day lifts your profile to others.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: How do active hazard scanning and Virginia's headlight rules work together to prevent crashes?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.memory_hook: Scanning spots risks, headlights show you
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: Scanning covers ahead, sides, and behind for missed risks, while headlights cover night and poor sight including wipers-on weather.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: When must you run headlights, and at what distances do you switch between low-beams and high-beams?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.memory_hook: Low inside two hundred, high five
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: Burn headlights from sunset to sunrise and from first fading light; take low-beams in lit towns, against oncoming traffic, and within two hundred feet behind another vehicle, reserving high-beams for highways clear of approaching vehicles within five hundred feet.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: Which driving settings call for low-beams versus open-highway high-beams?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.memory_hook: Low near traffic, high past five-hundred
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: Low-beams serve towns, oncoming meetings, and close following inside two hundred feet, while high-beams serve open highway free of oncoming vehicles inside five hundred feet.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: How should you steer and use your eyes—and what must you never flash—when oncoming high-beams blind you?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.memory_hook: Glance right edge, never flash back
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Faced with stubborn high-beams ahead, avert your stare toward the road edge, flick ahead to fix the other car's place, and repeat past it; never fire your own high-beams back.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: Why must you switch to low-beams, watch road-edge lines, and cut speed in fog?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: Fog throws your own beams back at you: drop to low-beams in thick fog, steer by edge markings, and slow since even thin fog warps distance judgment.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: How does handling an oncoming driver's high-beam glare compare with driving through thick fog?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.memory_hook: Glare glances right, fog drops beams
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Oncoming glare wants edge glances without high-beam revenge, while fog wants low-beams with edge-marking steering and slower speed.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: What three immediate adjustments should you make whenever visibility drops and pavement turns slick?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.memory_hook: Slow down, double gap, headlights on
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Answer fading sight and slick pavement by slowing first, doubling the normal gap ahead, and lighting the headlamps.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: When are wet roads most slippery during a rainstorm, and what lighting, washer, and puddle habits keep you safe?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.memory_hook: First half-hour slickest, avoid standing water
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: In rain, run low-beams, wipe light rain and drizzle with fluid ready since dry sprinkles smear, treat the first half-hour as slickest from oil mixing with water, and shun ponded water where the car can hydroplane and lose control.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Which parts of your vehicle must be cleared of snow and ice before driving, and what aids winter tire traction?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.memory_hook: Clear whole vehicle, add snow traction
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Strip every trace of snow and ice, roof, hood, tail, glass, mirrors, and all lamps, before rolling, since shed slabs menace others; fit snow tires or chains to grip and shorten stops.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: How does the peak slickness rule in rain contrast with pre-trip duties in snow and ice?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.memory_hook: Early rain oils, snow clears completely
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: Rain strikes slickest in the first half-hour of oil mixing, while snow demands full clearing before rolling and chains for grip.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: How should you slow and stop on packed snow or ice, and which road spots freeze earliest?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.memory_hook: Ease gas, gentle brakes, watch bridges
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Treat packed snow like ice: brake softly, shed speed before stops and turns, and to halt on slick sheets ease off the gas with gentle braking, since rolling front tires grip best and steady slowness beats hard braking; expect bridges and shade to ice first.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: Why do gentle braking and doubling your following gap belong together on icy pavement?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.memory_hook: Gentle braking needs doubled stopping room
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: Slick sheets want gentle braking with rolling front tires, matching the hazard rule that doubles the normal gap.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: What mental intent combined with traffic violations defines aggressive driving under Virginia law?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.memory_hook: Intent to harass plus traffic offense
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: Virginia law brands aggressive driving as aiming to harass, intimidate, injure, or obstruct someone while breaking traffic rules such as skipping stops, yields, control devices, or room for overtakers.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: What dangerous behaviors mark aggressive drivers, and how should you respond when targeted?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.memory_hook: Give room, skip eye contact, ignore
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: Aggressors run signs and signals, speed, tailgate, weave, pass right even on shoulders and unpaved edges, change lanes wildly, and gesture, scream, honk, and flash; counter by yielding space, refusing races and stares, and ignoring the noise.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: How does Virginia's legal definition of aggressive driving connect to the warning behaviors you see on the road?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.memory_hook: Law tests intent, road shows actions
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: The law defines aggression by harassing intent plus an offense, while the behavior list names the offenses from sign-running to shoulder passing.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: For how long can a Virginia court suspend your driver's license after an aggressive-driving conviction?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.memory_hook: Suspended ten days to six months
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: An aggressive-driving conviction can suspend a license for ten days or as long as six months.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: How does a smart driver's response to an aggressive motorist differ from a court's response upon conviction?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.memory_hook: Drivers give space, courts suspend licenses
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: Drivers answer aggressors with space and ignored noise, while courts answer convictions with ten days to six months of suspension.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: How often should you stop on a long drive, how long should a power nap run, and what overnight hours should you avoid?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.memory_hook: Break every two hours, skip overnight
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Cap long drives with a rest stop at least every two hours, nap ten to twenty minutes at a safe spot, share wheel time with a companion while a rested person drives, and shun the ten p.m. to six a.m. window.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: Which four common wake-up tricks fail against drowsiness, and what should happen if you spot a drowsy driver?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.memory_hook: Tricks fail; stop or report safely
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Cracked windows, gum, loud radio, and caffeine or energy drinks cannot fend off drowsiness; drowsy driving counts as impaired driving, and a drowsy driver you spot deserves a safe stop or a passenger's call to police with location, vehicle, and actions.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: How do proven defenses against drowsy driving contrast with popular roadside wake-up myths?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.memory_hook: Scheduled naps work, roadside gimmicks fail
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Real drowsy defense means two-hour breaks with short naps and rested drivers, while windows, gum, radio, and caffeine only pretend to help.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: What physical and lane-tracking clues warn that you are driving drowsy, and what pre-trip habits prevent it?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Yawns, nods, leaden lids, lost miles, skipped signs, stray lanes, shoulder runs, and rumble hits flag drowsiness, which clouds judgment and can drop you asleep; bank sleep first, skip booze and heavy meals, and mind dulling medicines.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: How do pre-trip fatigue prevention habits differ from on-road drowsiness warning signs?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.memory_hook: Bank sleep beforehand, spot yawns late
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Yawns, nods, and rumble strips warn of drowsiness already arrived, while sleep banking and meal care stop it before the trip.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: What BAC levels trigger DUI or illegal consumption for adults twenty-one and up versus drivers under twenty-one?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Drivers twenty-one and up reach DUI at point zero eight BAC or higher, with impairment alone able to convict lower; under twenty-one, point zero two up to point zero eight means illegal consumption and point zero eight or more means DUI; drug impairment draws DUI-grade penalties.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: How does Virginia's underage zero-tolerance BAC bracket compare with the standard adult DUI threshold?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.memory_hook: Point zero two underage, oh-eight DUI
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: Adults meet DUI at point-oh-eight, while drivers under twenty-one meet illegal consumption from point-oh-two and DUI at point-oh-eight.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: Between ten at night and two in the morning how many drivers are drunk, and how much does a single drink multiply crash risk?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.memory_hook: Three in ten drunk, sevenfold risk
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: From ten PM to two AM three of ten drivers run drunk, over a third coming from someone's home; nearly fifty percent of DUI arrests hit social-to-moderate drinkers; a lifetime alcohol-crash coin flip faces you; one drink dents vision, judgment, and coordination and multiplies crash odds seven times over sober.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: Which beer, wine, and liquor servings hold equal alcohol, what truly sobers you up, and when must you decide not to drive?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.memory_hook: Equal standard pours; only time sobers
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Twelve ounces of beer equal a liquor shot or a five-ounce wine glass; only passing time sobers, never coffee, cold showers, or workouts; since drink erodes the very judgment needed, lock in the no-drive call before the first sip.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: Why does switching from liquor shots to twelve-ounce beers or five-ounce wines fail to lower your single-drink crash risk?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: One drink already bends vision and judgment sevenfold, while equal pours of beer, liquor, and wine each bend it the same.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: What parallel truth links sobering up after drinking with recovering from drowsiness on a long drive?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.memory_hook: Only time sobers, only rest wakes
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Only time sobers a drinker past coffee and cold showers, matching how only real rest beats drowsiness past caffeine.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: What ride plan belongs before any drinking event, and why is combining one drink with aspirin or cold medicine dangerous?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.memory_hook: Book sober ride; mixing multiplies effects
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: Before a drinking event, book a sober ride via alternate transport or a sober driver; alcohol stacked on drugs multiplies both, so a single drink atop even aspirin or cold medicine can hit like several.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: How does arranging a sober ride beforehand protect you from the multiplier effect of alcohol and everyday medicines?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.memory_hook: Prebooked rides beat surprise pill multipliers
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: A booked sober ride dodges the whole question, while one drink stacked on pills can multiply into several.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: Which legal remedies—alongside marijuana past age twenty-one—can impair driving and require checking labels or a pharmacist?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.memory_hook: Cold, allergy, nerve remedies, and marijuana
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Nearly every drug can dull driving, legal ones included: headache, hay fever, cold, allergy, and nerve pills, syrups, drops, sprays, and tablets slow you; marijuana stays DUI-illegal behind the wheel past twenty-one; read labels, quiz your pharmacist or doctor, and treat no drug as harmless.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: How do illegal street drugs, pharmacy cold or allergy meds, and adult-use marijuana compare behind the wheel?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.memory_hook: Street, pharmacy, and cannabis all impair
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: Street drugs impair, and so do headache, cold, and allergy remedies plus legal marijuana behind the wheel.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: When is using a phone or computer acceptable behind the wheel, and what should you do before handling any distraction?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Driving wants your whole attention: shelve phones, computers, and like devices except to report a crash or emergency, and pull fully over before any distracting act.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: When does Virginia law prohibit holding a wireless device, and under what conditions may you use phone navigation?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.memory_hook: Never hold driving; hands-free nav only
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Virginia bars holding a phone or wireless device at the wheel except in a driver emergency or while lawfully parked or stopped; navigation use stands only while entering nothing and holding nothing.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: What separates illegal phone handling from lawful GPS navigation while driving in Virginia?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.memory_hook: Holding breaks law, hands-free nav passes
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: Holding any wireless device breaks the law outside emergencies and parked stops, while hands-free navigation without typing stays legal.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: Roughly what share of Virginia crashes stem from distraction, and how does distraction combine with teen inexperience?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.memory_hook: Seventeen percent crashes, stolen reaction seconds
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Distraction causes roughly seventeen percent of Virginia crashes: the straying car enters peril, recognition lags precious seconds, and an emergency move follows; young distracteds add weak control, tailgating, and yield failures to raw inexperience.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: What three practical habits keep distraction out of the driver's seat from start to finish?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.memory_hook: Preset controls, eyes up, phone untouched
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Dodge distraction by fixing eyes on the road with hands on the wheel, presetting every control before rolling, and leaving the cell phone alone.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: How do presetting cabin controls and leaving your phone alone counter the chain reaction behind Virginia's distraction crashes?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Distraction eats recognition seconds behind seventeen percent of crashes, while eyes-up, preset, phone-down habits buy them back.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: What scene-safety, vehicle-clearing, injured-care, and police-reporting rules apply right after a crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.memory_hook: Stop safely, clear drivable, call police
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: In a crash, halt at the scene or near it without blocking traffic, clear drivable cars when nobody is hurt and it is safe, step out shielded by your car, help the hurt without moving them absent training or fire danger, and summon police fast since property, injury, and fatal crashes all require reports.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: How does your immediate roadside duty in a minor drivable fender-bender differ from a crash with injured occupants?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: Drivable and unhurt means clear the road at once, while hurt occupants mean shield, aid, and summon without moving them.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: What details must drivers exchange after a crash, and what injury or dollar threshold triggers an officer's DMV crash report?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.memory_hook: Swap full details; three-thousand triggers DMV
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Trade names, addresses, license and plate numbers, injured and witness contacts, and owners' insurance policy numbers on the spot, ring your insurer at once, and know officers file DMV reports on any injury or death and damage over three thousand dollars, entered on every involved driver's record.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: If you hit an unoccupied parked car or property and cannot find the owner, what note details and police deadline apply?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.memory_hook: Leave detailed note, report within twenty-four
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: After striking an empty car or property, hunt reasonably for its owner, else pin an easy-to-find note carrying your name, phone, date, time, and damage sketch, and still tell police within twenty-four hours.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: How do your legal duties after colliding with another driver compare with striking an unattended vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.memory_hook: Swap papers, or note plus police
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: Manned crashes trade papers and call insurers on the spot, while empty-car strikes leave name-phone-time notes plus a twenty-four-hour police report.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: When are Virginia deer strikes likeliest, how should you react if impact is unavoidable, and whom do you notify after hitting one?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.memory_hook: Brake straight in lane, never swerve
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Tens of thousands of Virginia deer, elk, and bear strikes land yearly: stay sharp at dusk and dawn through fall, brake for grouped animals near the road, horn them off, and when contact is certain hold the lane under firm braking to a controlled stop instead of swerving, then report a large-animal hit to police.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.front: How does the threshold for an officer's DMV crash-record filing compare with reporting a large-animal collision?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.memory_hook: Over three-thousand DMV, animal hits police
sec11-card-sec11-R12.expected_back: Injury, death, or three-thousand-dollar damage routes to DMV records, while any large-animal strike routes to law enforcement.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.front: How should your response to deer standing near the roadside differ from when a deer leaps directly in front of you?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.memory_hook: Slow and honk early, brake straight
sec11-card-sec11-R13.expected_back: Near deer want slowing, horns, and group wariness, while certain contact wants straight-line braking with no swerve.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: How does Virginia DMV deliver licenses, how soon must you report an address move, and what does the post office do?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: Licenses arrive by mail only, never over DMV counters; movers must tell DMV within thirty days since the post office will not forward licenses and returns them instead.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: Why do mail-only license delivery and postal non-forwarding make Virginia's thirty-day address rule critical?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: Licenses come only by mail, while address moves must reach DMV within thirty days since mail will not forward them.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: After moving to Virginia, how many days do you have to get a driver's license versus titling and plating your car—and how are plates worn?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: New Virginians owe a state license within sixty days and title, registration, and plates within thirty days, worn front and rear with month-year decals in their plate slots except on permanent plates.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: Which new-resident Virginia requirement gives sixty days, and which requires action within thirty days?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: Newcomers owe licenses in sixty days but plates in thirty, front and rear with decals.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: Where must your state registration card stay whenever you drive, and when is local city or county registration also required?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: Keep the registration card aboard every drive, and register locally too where your city or county demands it.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: How does carrying your state registration card differ from registering a vehicle with a local city or county?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: The card rides along every drive, while locality registration rides only where cities demand.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: How often must a Virginia vehicle pass a safety inspection, and when is an emissions check required too?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: Pass the yearly safety inspection and wear its sticker, plus emissions testing where your locality orders it.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: How often should you inspect tire tread, and how do you grip the coin to begin the penny check?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: Monthly or pre-trip, start the penny test by pinching Lincoln's body between thumb and finger.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: How does Virginia's official safety inspection schedule compare with your own penny tire-tread checks?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: The state inspects yearly with stickers, while drivers inspect tires monthly starting with the penny pinch.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: How did Virginia's minimum liability coverage numbers change on January 1, 2022, and whose driving records can affect premiums?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: Registration wants liability from a Virginia-authorized carrier or the five hundred dollars uninsured fee; minimums run twenty-five thousand dollars per person, fifty thousand dollars per crash, twenty thousand dollars property before Jan. one, two thousand twenty-two, and thirty thousand dollars, sixty thousand dollars, twenty thousand dollars after, with household driving-age records able to price premiums.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: Which two coverage numbers rose when Virginia moved from pre-2022 policies to post-2022 liability minimums?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: Pre-two thousand twenty-two policies floor at twenty-five, fifty, twenty, while post-two thousand twenty-two floors rise to thirty, sixty, twenty.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: What does the five-hundred-dollar uninsured-vehicle fee actually buy, and what must you surrender before canceling insurance—even on a broken parked car?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: The fee buys no coverage, only a one-year right to run; insure across the whole registration span even parked or dead, and surrender plates plus registration before dropping coverage.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: How does carrying a liability policy differ from paying Virginia's five-hundred-dollar uninsured-vehicle fee?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: Liability or five hundred dollars buys registration, but only insurance buys coverage while the fee buys a one-year pass.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: What payment and multi-year filing must you complete if caught without insurance and without having paid the uninsured fee?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: Caught bare without the fee, driving dies until a six hundred dollars noncompliance payment or plan plus an insurer certificate riding three years past reinstatement.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: How does turning in plates before canceling insurance compare with getting caught uninsured without paying the fee?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: Dropping coverage starts with surrendering plates, while getting caught bare starts a six-hundred-dollar and three-year certificate climb.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: Who qualifies to register to vote on a Virginia DMV application, and what must felons or people adjudicated mentally incompetent obtain first?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: DMV doubles as voter registrar via the license form for citizens residing in Virginia and eighteen by the next general election, with felons and the incompetent needing circuit-court restoration first.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: How do you sign up to donate organs, eyes, and tissue at DMV, when is your choice legally binding, and whom should you tell?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: Check yes on license, permit, or ID forms to donate organs, eyes, and tissue; eighteen-plus decisions bind, under-eighteen wishes bow to parents and guardians, and every donor should broadcast the choice to kin.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.front: How does the age-eighteen rule work differently for DMV voter registration versus DMV organ-donor consent?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.expected_back: Voting wants citizenship, residency, and eighteen by election day, while donation binds at eighteen and bows to parents below.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Which three screenings can Virginia licensing include, and who determines which ones apply to you?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Virginia testing can include a vision screening, a two-part knowledge exam, and a road skills test, and a DMV representative tells each applicant which tests apply.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Holding a valid driver license from which U.S. or four international places excuses you from Virginia's knowledge exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: You must take the knowledge exam unless you hold a valid driver license from another United States state, Canada, Germany, France, or the Republic of Korea.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: How is Virginia's two-part knowledge exam delivered, what three topics does it test, and where do items come from?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: The two-part knowledge exam runs on a computer and covers traffic signs, motor vehicle laws, and safe driving, with every question drawn from this manual.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: How many traffic-sign items are in part one of Virginia's knowledge exam, and how many must you get right?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: Part one holds ten traffic sign questions, and you must answer all ten correctly before part two is allowed.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: What format is part two of Virginia's knowledge exam, and what minimum score passes it?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: Part two is general-knowledge multiple choice, and passing it requires at least eighty percent correct.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: How does the required passing score on part one compare with part two of Virginia's knowledge exam?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: Part one demands a perfect ten-for-ten on traffic signs before part two opens, while part two passes at eighty percent on general multiple choice.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Which two official places offer a sample Virginia knowledge exam before you visit the DMV?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: A sample knowledge exam appears in Section eight of this manual and on the DMV website.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: Who should customers with disabilities or special needs notify when they need application or testing assistance?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Customers with special needs or disabilities should tell DMV staff at any location when they need help with applications or testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: How many knowledge attempts are allowed per business day, and when are personal translators barred?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: Only one attempt is allowed per business day; the exam comes in an audio version and many languages including American Sign Language, so translators are barred where those are offered.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Why do Virginia's audio, ASL, and multilingual computer versions eliminate using a translator?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: The exam offers an audio version and many languages including American Sign Language, yet translators stay barred wherever those versions exist.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: Which four forms of assistance, content sharing, or phone use are strictly banned during testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: While testing you may not get help, help another person, seek or share questions or answers, or use a cell phone.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: How does Virginia treat giving versus receiving help, and hunting items beforehand versus sharing them afterward?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: Receiving help and giving help are two separately banned acts, and seeking questions beforehand and sharing them afterward are banned as well.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: How long must an applicant younger than eighteen wait after failing the knowledge exam—for example after failing January 1?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: A failing applicant under age eighteen must wait a full fifteen days before retaking; failing on January one means January seventeen is the earliest retake.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: What educational requirement kicks in if you fail the Virginia knowledge exam three times?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: After three knowledge-exam failures, a fourth attempt requires completing and passing the classroom part of driver education.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: Instead of full classroom driver ed, what shorter course option can applicants eighteen or older use after three failures?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: Drivers age eighteen or older may instead finish an eight-hour DMV-approved course based on this manual, taken after the third failure at a training school or online, and retake after giving DMV the completion certificate.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Under what prior condition may an applicant younger than eighteen take the eight-hour manual course?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: Drivers younger than eighteen may use that manual course only after finishing classroom driver education, and must show the classroom certificate to the training school first.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How do Virginia's under-eighteen retake wait and post-third-failure course rules work for minors versus adults?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: An applicant younger than eighteen must wait fifteen full days after a failed knowledge exam. After three failures, a fourth attempt requires passing classroom driver education or a DMV-approved eight-hour manual course. Adults may use that course; younger applicants need prior classroom completion. The manual course must be completed after the third failure, and its certificate goes to DMV.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: After three knowledge failures, how does access to the eight-hour manual course differ for adults versus minors?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: After three failures, adults may take the manual course directly, while minors may take it only after already completing classroom driver education.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: Valid licenses from which U.S. states or five international jurisdictions waive Virginia's road skills check?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: The road skills test is required unless you hold a valid license from another United States state, Canada, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea, or Taiwan.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: Who provides the road-check car, which vehicle type is banned, and what tags and safety gear must work?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: You must supply the test vehicle, which cannot be an autocycle and must show a valid inspection sticker, plates, registration card and decals, plus working brakes, belts, horn, lights, signals, mirrors, and speedometer.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Which two alternative forms prove your readiness before the road examiner lets you start?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: The examiner requires either an accepted driver-education completion certificate or a completed behind-the-wheel checklist on DMV form CSMA nineteen, with a licensed driver certifying supervised practice and permit-rule compliance.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Can you take Virginia's road skills check without either a driver-ed certificate or form CSMA 19?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: The examiner accepts either a driver-education completion certificate or a supervised-practice checklist on form CSMA nineteen, with one of the two always required.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: Where do applicants younger than eighteen take their road skills check, and what guides home-schooled teens?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Applicants under eighteen take the road skills test inside their driver-education course at a public, private, or commercial school, while home-schooled applicants follow information sheet HS three.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: At age eighteen or older, what two tracks unlock your first road check, and who administers each?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: At eighteen or older you must hold the learner permit for sixty days before the first road test or finish approved driver education; the school tests driver-education students while DMV staff test permit holders.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: How do road-check options differ between applicants under eighteen and applicants eighteen or older?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: Minors take the road test inside their driver-education course, while adults choose between a sixty-day permit hold with DMV testing or an approved course with school testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: What daily cap, single-failure wait, and three-failure requirement govern DMV road skills attempts?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: The road test allows one attempt per business day; after a failure you wait two days, and after three DMV failures the fourth attempt waits until you pass the in-vehicle part at an approved school and deliver the certificate to DMV, with that completion dated after the third failure.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: How does the consequence of one DMV road-check failure compare with a third DMV failure?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: One road failure costs two waiting days, while a third DMV failure costs the applicant an in-vehicle training course before any fourth attempt.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: What happens during DMV vision screening, and what happens if you do not pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: Vision screening means reading letters or numbers in a machine; it is not a medical exam, and failing it can send you to an eye care professional.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: What license code applies if you need glasses or contacts to pass, and how can laser surgery remove it?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: If glasses or contacts are needed to pass screening, you must wear them while driving with a C restriction on the license; after laser surgery the restriction lifts by passing screening unaided at a customer service center or filing Vision Screening Report MED four.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: What puts the C restriction onto a Virginia license, and what two ways clear it after laser correction?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: Needing glasses to pass screening adds the C restriction, while laser surgery removes it only through a fresh unaided pass or a filed MED four report.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: What visual acuity and horizontal field of vision are required for an unrestricted Virginia license?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: An unrestricted license needs at least twenty over forty vision in one or both eyes plus at least one hundred ten degrees of horizontal vision in one or both eyes, or a comparable field measurement.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: What acuity and horizontal field—including single-eye nose and temple angles—qualify for daylight-only driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: Daylight-only driving needs at least twenty over seventy vision and at least seventy degrees horizontal; with one eye that means thirty degrees or better toward the nose and forty degrees or better toward the temple, or a comparable measurement.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How do acuity and horizontal field numbers compare between unrestricted and daylight-only licenses?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: Unrestricted vision needs twenty-forty acuity with one hundred ten degrees of field, while daylight-only needs twenty-seventy acuity with seventy degrees of field.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: Between which exact sunrise and sunset buffers may a daylight-only license holder drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: Daylight-only permission covers only the period from a half-hour after sunrise to a half-hour before sunset.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: What driving rules attach to a C restriction versus a daylight-only restriction?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: A license marked C requires the glasses or contacts needed to pass vision screening whenever you drive. A daylight-only license permits driving beginning thirty minutes after sunrise and ending thirty minutes before sunset.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: Which DMV publication covers licensing rules for drivers who wear bioptic telescopic lenses?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: Drivers wearing bioptic telescopic lenses should read DMV publication MED forty-four on licensing information for bioptic lens wearers.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: How does DMV form MED 4 differ in purpose from DMV publication MED 44?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: Form MED four reports a vision screening result, while publication MED forty-four informs bioptic telescopic lens wearers about licensing.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: Is cutting across a parking lot to skip a red light legal, and whose command overrides every sign or light?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Signals, signs, and markings keep traffic orderly; cutting through a lot or field to dodge them is illegal, and a police officer's direction overrules every sign and signal.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: Which five groups of road users are legally bound by Virginia traffic signals?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: Traffic signals bind drivers, motorcycle riders, bicyclists, moped riders, and pedestrians alike.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: Where must your vehicle stop at a steady red light when a stop line is painted versus when none exists?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: At a red light, stop fully at the stop line, or before the intersection or crosswalk where no line exists, and stay stopped while red unless a turn is allowed.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: What stop, scan, and yield steps are required before turning right on a steady red light?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: A right turn on red needs a full stop first, then a both-ways look with the right-of-way yielded to pedestrians and traffic, watching for motorcycles, bicycles, and mopeds.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Which two intersection controls forbid making a right turn on red?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: No right turn on red is allowed where No Turn on Red signs stand or where a red arrow points right.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Between which street types—and under what conditions—is a left turn on red legal in Virginia?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: A left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street after a full stop and yield, and never where signs or a red left arrow forbid it.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: How do the street requirements and bans compare for turning right on red versus left on red?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: After a full stop and yielding to pedestrians and other traffic, a right turn on red is permitted unless a No Turn on Red sign or rightward red arrow prohibits it. A left turn on red requires a one-way street leading onto another one-way street, the same stop and yield, and no prohibiting sign or leftward red arrow.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: What does a steady red arrow command in Virginia, and what sole exception allows turning?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: A red arrow means stop and stay stopped in that direction unless Right on Red Arrow After Stop or Left on Red Arrow After Stop signs are posted; Virginia otherwise bans turns at red arrows.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: Why shouldn't you assume Virginia's red-light and red-arrow turn rules apply when driving out of state?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Red-light and red-arrow turn rules differ by state, so learn the local law before turning on red outside Virginia.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: How do you handle a flashing red intersection light, and what rule applies at a railroad flashing red?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: At a flashing red light, stop fully, yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians, and go only when clear; at a railroad crossing, always stop even with no train in sight.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: What three steps let you proceed in the direction of a flashing red arrow?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: At a flashing red arrow, stop fully, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and move in the arrow direction only when clear.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: How does a steady red arrow differ from a flashing red arrow in Virginia?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: A steady red arrow requires waiting unless a posted sign specifically permits that turn after stopping. A flashing red arrow requires a full stop and yielding to opposing vehicles and pedestrians; proceed in its direction only when clear.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: How does a steady circular red light differ from a flashing red light for straight-through traffic?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: At steady red, make a full stop and wait while red continues, except for a permitted turn. At flashing red, stop fully, yield to approaching vehicles and pedestrians, and continue only after the path is clear.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: What must you do at a steady yellow light or arrow depending on whether you can stop safely?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: A steady yellow light or arrow warns the signal is changing: stop if you have not entered, pass through cautiously if stopping is unsafe or you are already inside, and never speed up.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: What road condition and driving response belong to a flashing yellow light?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution, marking a spot with higher-than-normal hazard.
