sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Staying out of red-painted transit lanes avoids citations and keeps city buses moving clear of private car queues.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: How are HOV lanes marked and separated, who qualifies during restricted hours, and how do barrier lanes operate?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Always read overhead signs for passenger minimums, restricted hours, and time-of-day direction shifts before entering diamond-marked lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: Besides high-occupancy carpool corridors, what other restricted travel lane can a painted diamond designate?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Because white diamonds mark any preferential lane, checking accompanying roadside signs tells you whether carpools or only transit buses qualify.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: How does driver eligibility differ between diamond-marked HOV lanes and red bus-only lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: High-occupancy cars, motorcycles, and clean-fuel tags qualify for HOV diamonds, whereas red transit paint shuts out private vehicles.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: What three hazard categories do portable and overhead message boards report, and how must you treat them?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Live electronic boards post real-time crash closures and weather detours that override your routine commute habits.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: How should you steer and manage speed when rumble strip warnings appear ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel onto the shoulder or opposing lane just to dodge harmless tire vibration risks a rollover or collision.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: How does your response to an electronic message board compare with crossing transverse rumble strips?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Message panels give routing commands to execute, while grooved asphalt delivers a tactile wake-up call before a stop or toll.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: What speed ceiling and vehicle types carry slow-moving vehicle signs, and how must you react?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Closing at fifty-five miles per hour on a tractor crawling under twenty-five shrinks the gap shockingly fast unless you lift off early.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: Which transponder works statewide at Virginia tolls, how do purple-logo and cash lanes split, and what hazards lurk?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Toll plazas mix last-second lane weavers with walking plaza staff, making cautious speed reductions vital in every booth approach.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: Why must you never stop or back up if you enter a high-speed E-ZPass lane without a transponder?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Slamming brakes inside an open-road highway toll chute guarantees a violent rear-end crash over a billable mail notice.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: How do purple-logo booths, cash lanes, and high-speed transponder chutes each handle drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Sorting your payment lane early prevents panic maneuvers, and rolling straight through an accidental express entry protects everyone.
sec05-card-sec05-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Purple tags, cash pays, express rolls

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: After checking local ordinances, what curbside rules usually pair with white, yellow, and red paint?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Leaving your vehicle unattended at a yellow loading curb or halting beside red fire-lane paint invites an instant tow or ticket.
sec05-card-sec05-F28.must_match_memory_hook: White passengers, yellow loading, red zero

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: Which painted curb lets passengers hop in, which requires staying with cargo, and which forbids stopping?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Test questions frequently swap white passenger zones with yellow driver-attended freight curbs, so anchor each color's job.
sec05-card-sec05-R12.must_match_memory_hook: White dropoff, yellow stay, red none

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: Which lane starts and finishes a right turn, how early do you signal, and what scanning and braking rules apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Signaling three or four seconds out and hugging the right curb prevents cyclists or cars from sneaking inside.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: From which lane into which lane do you turn left, how should your front wheels point while waiting, and whom do you yield to?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Keeping front tires straight while waiting stops a rear-end bump from shoving your car into oncoming traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Contrast the starting and ending lane rules for a standard right turn versus a standard left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Swinging wide across multiple lanes mid-turn sideswipes parallel turners or fast oncoming traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: When two opposing vehicles both signal left turns at an intersection, how should they pass each other?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Turning in front of each other keeps sightlines clear instead of hooking blindly behind the other car.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: Which two signs must you look for before a U-turn, where are town or business U-turns restricted, and what about highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Even a No Left Turn sign bans a U-turn, and highway speeds make mid-road turnarounds lethal.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: How many of the three U-turn checks — prohibitive signs, mid-block town streets, or highways — does it take to make a U-turn illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Drivers get ticketed mid-block in town even without a posted sign because town U-turns belong strictly at intersections.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: Walk through the four signal, stop, yield, and target-lane steps for making a U-turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Most sedan turning circles swing wide, so aiming cleanly into the opposite outside right-hand lane matches your arc.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: How does a U-turn's stopping and target-lane rule differ from a normal left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Normal green-light lefts yield without a mandatory halt into the inside lane, whereas U-turns stop first and finish outside.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: Which maneuvers legally require turn or hand signals, must you signal on an empty street, and what follows the move?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Signaling even when the street looks deserted protects unseen cyclists or walkers, and canceling stops false cues.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: How many seconds and feet before a turn should you signal — and what mistake by side-street drivers should you watch for?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Side-street drivers seeing your blinker may pull out early thinking you are turning into their driveway.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: When does your turn signal go on before a maneuver, and what must happen once you finish?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Cruising down the block with a forgotten blinker tricks cross-street drivers into pulling directly across your bow.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: Using your left arm out the window, which positions signal a left turn, a right turn, and slowing or stopping?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Knowing standard left-arm positions lets you signal legally if a bulb burns out or read cyclists ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: Match each left-arm position — straight out, bent upward, and bent downward — to its driving meaning?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: DMV exams love pairing bent-upward versus bent-downward because new drivers confuse right turns with braking.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: What does steering over-correction do to your rear wheels, how should you enter curves, and how do you recover if you veer off?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Yanking the wheel back sharply kicks the rear tires sideways into a spin or rollover across oncoming lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: What steering mistake slides the rear wheels outward, and what three calm habits bring you safely back on track?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Aiming your eyes down your target lane while easing speed lets gentle steering bring tires smoothly over the edge.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: Where do you position inside your lane and keep open buffers to build a protective space cushion?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Staying centered with generous room front and back gives everyone space to brake or pass cleanly.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: On dry pavement, how many following seconds match under thirty-five, thirty-five to forty-five, and forty-six to seventy — and above seventy?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Virginia scales dry following distance across three speed brackets, and past seventy miles per hour the formula fails completely.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: Pair each Virginia following-distance count — two, three, four, and none — with its exact speed bracket?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Memorize those exact cutoffs at thirty-five, forty-five, and seventy because Virginia tests speed-band seconds heavily.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: How do you measure your following seconds with a fixed roadside object, and which four conditions call for extra seconds?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Reaching the landmark too soon proves you are tailgating, and rain, heavy traffic, rough roads, or worn cars need more.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: Roughly how fast do hands versus feet react — and which human and vehicle factors stretch perception and stopping?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Steering reacts slightly quicker than braking, while fatigue, meds, distraction, speed, road grip, and weight stretch total stops.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: How does average hand reaction time compare with average foot reaction time before impairment delays even start?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Moving your foot from gas to brake takes longer than turning your wrists, and drowsiness slows both.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Behind which vehicles and in which road or traffic situations must you stretch your normal following gap?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Extra room behind sight-blocking rigs, fragile two-wheelers, off-ramps, or tailgaters lets you brake gently instead of slamming.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: How does counting past a fixed landmark work alongside knowing when to add extra seconds?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Counting checks your dry baseline, while big trucks, motorcycles, bad weather, exits, and tailgaters push that target higher.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: What brake mistake must you avoid when tailgated, how do you shake a tailgater, and how do you help normal followers?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Brake-checking invites a rear-end crash, whereas changing lanes or lightly tapping brake lights warns them safely.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: Contrast your response to an aggressive tailgater with everyday courteous driving for cars behind you?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Stepping aside clears a tailgater off your bumper, while steady speed and early brake taps keep everyday followers calm.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: How many seconds — or city blocks — ahead should you aim your focus, and how should your eyes work the scene?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Keeping eyes sweeping side-to-side twenty to thirty seconds ahead catches signs, signals, cars, and walkers early.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: Which parked-car clues warn someone is pulling out — and what extra hazards appear on rural roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Puffing tailpipes, backup lights, or angled front tires telegraph pull-outs, while country crests hide slow farm gear.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: Which scan order checks an intersection — and why that side first — plus how often and when do you check mirrors?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Cross traffic from your left enters your lane first, and ten-second mirror sweeps track closing rear traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: Put Virginia's three scanning habits together — forward focus seconds, rearview mirror interval, and intersection head scan?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Locking in twenty-to-thirty ahead, ten-second mirror checks, and left-right-left corners covers all four sides.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: How should you aim your inside and side mirrors, and what physical check clears blind spots before lane changes or passes?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Angling side mirrors outward until your car's flank barely shows shrinks blind zones, and a shoulder glance clears the rest.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: What two speed adjustments keep you from lingering inside another driver's blind spot?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Cruising beside a neighbor's rear quarter panel leaves you invisible when they swerve or change lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: Contrast how you manage your own vehicle's blind spots with how you handle another driver's blind spots?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Proper mirrors and head turns solve your blind zones, while pacing ahead or behind keeps you visible to others.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Who counts as a vulnerable road user in Virginia, what driving conduct around them is illegal, and what duty applies?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Walkers, riders, skaters, scooter or wheelchair users, and animals have zero steel cage, making careless driving around them illegal.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: Where must you stay extra alert for walkers, and what turning, passing, and lane-clearing rules protect crosswalks?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Passing a car stopped at a crosswalk strikes hidden pedestrians stepping out in front of their bumper.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: For whom must Virginia drivers come to a full stop, and what criminal charge hits failing to stop and causing serious injury or death?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Failing to halt for a white-cane, guide-dog, or lawful crossing pedestrian and causing severe harm brings criminal prosecution.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How does waiting out a crossing while turning pair with Virginia's full-stop rule and serious-injury penalty?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Rolling turns crowd walkers still in the street, and blowing past cane or lawful crossings risks Class one misdemeanor charges.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: Where may bicyclists ride on Virginia roads and lanes, which highways bar them, and where may they approach from either direction?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Cyclists legally take the full lane when narrow width or left turns require it and ride two-way on paths or sidewalks.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: How much side clearance must you give when passing a bicyclist, when must you change lanes, and may cars enter marked bike lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Squeezing past closer than three feet buffets riders off balance, and marked bike lanes stay off-limits even for passing.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: Balance what Virginia grants bicyclists on the road against the three space rules owed by drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Respecting a rider's centered lane position means changing lanes cleanly with three feet of room while keeping bike lanes empty.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: At which six everyday driving or parking moments must you scan specifically for bicycles — and what bike move should you expect?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Slim bicycle frames vanish behind pillars before pull-outs, lane shifts, turns, backing, opening doors, and intersections.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: In what share of car-motorcycle crashes did the car driver miss seeing the bike in time — and why does that happen?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Human brains scan habitually for wide four-wheeled silhouettes, overlooking narrow motorcycles until impact is unavoidable.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: Pair why bicycles need checks at six maneuver points with why motorcycles demand double looks?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Quiet bicycles slip beside doors and curbs unseen, while narrow motorcycles fool distance judgment across intersections.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: What lane-sharing, dry following-time, wet following-time, and swerve rules apply behind a motorcycle?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Riders swerve inside their full lane width to dodge potholes that cars straddle, and slick roads double your cushion.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: Summarize the four space and time protections Virginia gives a motorcyclist ahead of your car?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Motorcycles stop briskly without big brake-light bars, making tailgating or crowding beside them inside one lane dangerous.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: How many crossings span Norfolk's seven-point-four-mile light rail The Tide, and what gate, track, and turning rules apply?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Quiet electric streetcars arrive from either direction anytime, so never circle gates or stop, pass, or shift on rails.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: Separate what light-rail crossings strictly forbid from the three habits they require?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Going around lowered gates or halting on tracks invites silent train impacts unless you verify far-side clearance first.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: What top-speed band defines low-speed vehicles, which roads and drivers may run them, and do golf carts qualify?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: True low-speed vehicles carry federal safety gear, registration, and insurance on thirty-five-or-under streets, unlike golf carts.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: Contrast a street-legal Virginia low-speed vehicle's speed and road limit against a golf cart?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Exam distractors lump neighborhood golf carts in with registered twenty-one-to-twenty-five low-speed vehicles.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: How do trucks, tractor-trailers, buses, and RVs handle compared with cars, and where sit their No-Zones?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Extra length, height, width, and mass stretch acceleration, turning, and braking while hiding cars on sides, front, and rear.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: Why are side No-Zones so dangerous on trucks, buses, and RVs — and what mirror rule tells whether the driver sees you?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Wide-swinging trailers sweep across side blind zones whenever you cannot spot the driver's face inside their side mirror.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What two sight losses and crash trap hit drivers who tailgate inside a truck's rear No-Zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Riding right behind trailer doors hides you from the trucker and blocks your view ahead when traffic halts abruptly.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: Why do front No-Zones punish cutting in early — including truck stopping ratio, sixty-five-foot length, half-mile pass, and mirror cue?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Loaded sixty-five-foot rigs need nearly double car stopping distance, so wait until the entire cab fills your rearview.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: Match the side, rear, and front truck No-Zones to the specific crash hazard each creates?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Side zones crush cars in wide turns, rear zones trap tailgaters at sudden stops, and front zones punish early cut-ins.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: How far ahead and behind can large-vehicle blind spots reach, and what must you never do beside a turning rig?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Trucks swing left before turning right, crushing anyone who squeezes between their trailer and the curb.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: Contrast safe positioning when merging ahead of an overtaken truck versus approaching a turning truck?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Overtaking ends with the full cab in your mirror at steady speed, while turning rigs forbid squeezing alongside.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: What hitching and mirror gear do light or medium trailers need, and how much does towing multiply driving effort?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Hitched weight doubles the room and effort needed to accelerate, pass, turn, and stop while adding No-Zones.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: How does towing a trailer compare with a large truck's stopping demand?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Whether pulling a weekend camper or sharing lanes with a semi, expect roughly twice normal car braking demand.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: What mistake causes most backing crashes, and what posture and speed should you use when reversing?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Relying only on mirrors hides children and cross-traffic in wide rear blind zones right behind your bumper.
sec10-card-sec10-F01.must_match_memory_hook: Turn right, look back, reverse slowly

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: Which three groups of road users must you check for before opening a parked car door?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Flinging a street-side door open blindly can knock an approaching cyclist directly into moving traffic.
sec10-card-sec10-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Scan cars, cyclists, and walkers first

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How does the visual check required to reverse a car differ from the check before stepping out?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Reversing moves two tons of steel through blind spots, whereas exiting checks approaching traffic before unlatching a door.
sec10-card-sec10-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Twist to reverse, scan before exiting

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: How close to a curb should you park, and which road sides are legal on two-way versus one-way streets?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Parking wide of the curb narrows active travel lanes and clips passing mirrors on tight city blocks.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: Why do mail-only license delivery and postal non-forwarding make Virginia's thirty-day address rule critical?

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: After moving to Virginia, how many days do you have to get a driver's license versus titling and plating your car—and how are plates worn?

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: Which new-resident Virginia requirement gives sixty days, and which requires action within thirty days?

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: Where must your state registration card stay whenever you drive, and when is local city or county registration also required?

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: How does carrying your state registration card differ from registering a vehicle with a local city or county?

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: How often must a Virginia vehicle pass a safety inspection, and when is an emissions check required too?

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: How often should you inspect tire tread, and how do you grip the coin to begin the penny check?

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: How does Virginia's official safety inspection schedule compare with your own penny tire-tread checks?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: Tires wear bald long before twelve months pass, so pair your annual state inspection sticker with monthly and pre-trip penny checks.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: How did Virginia's minimum liability coverage numbers change on January 1, 2022, and whose driving records can affect premiums?

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: Which two coverage numbers rose when Virginia moved from pre-2022 policies to post-2022 liability minimums?

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: What does the five-hundred-dollar uninsured-vehicle fee actually buy, and what must you surrender before canceling insurance—even on a broken parked car?
