sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: How does carrying a liability policy differ from paying Virginia's five-hundred-dollar uninsured-vehicle fee?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: Both satisfy DMV registration, yet only liability insurance pays crash claims while the five-hundred-dollar fee leaves you personally liable.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: What payment and multi-year filing must you complete if caught without insurance and without having paid the uninsured fee?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Driving and registration stay suspended until you pay—or arrange—the six-hundred-dollar noncompliance fee and keep insurer proof filed for three years.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: How does turning in plates before canceling insurance compare with getting caught uninsured without paying the fee?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Turning in plates and registration before canceling costs nothing extra, whereas getting caught bare triggers six hundred dollars and three years of filings.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: Who qualifies to register to vote on a Virginia DMV application, and what must felons or people adjudicated mentally incompetent obtain first?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: U.S. citizens living in Virginia who turn eighteen by the next general election qualify—once any felony or competency disqualification is restored.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: How do you sign up to donate organs, eyes, and tissue at DMV, when is your choice legally binding, and whom should you tell?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Checking yes at eighteen or older makes your donor wish legally binding—under eighteen requires parent or guardian consent—so tell your family.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: How does the age-eighteen rule work differently for DMV voter registration versus DMV organ-donor consent?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: Future eighteen-year-olds can register if eighteen by general election day, whereas organ-donor checkboxes require parental approval until your eighteenth birthday.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: Which three screenings can Virginia licensing include, and who determines which ones apply to you?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Every applicant's age and prior license history differ, so DMV staff confirm your exact screening mix at check-in.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Holding a valid driver license from which U.S. or four international places excuses you from Virginia's knowledge exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Reciprocity agreements waive the written computer exam for valid license holders from U.S. states plus those four nations.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: How is Virginia's two-part knowledge exam delivered, what three topics does it test, and where do items come from?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Studying the Virginia Driver's Manual covers every single item because nothing comes from outside its pages.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: How many traffic-sign items are in part one of Virginia's knowledge exam, and how many must you get right?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Missing even a single sign in part one ends your attempt immediately before part two ever opens.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: What format is part two of Virginia's knowledge exam, and what minimum score passes it?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Once you sweep all ten signs cleanly, hitting at least eighty percent on general multiple-choice rules clears part two.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: How does the required passing score on part one compare with part two of Virginia's knowledge exam?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Traffic signs leave zero room for error on roads or on screen, whereas general rules allow a twenty-percent cushion.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: Which two official places offer a sample Virginia knowledge exam before you visit the DMV?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Running through the manual's back-section sample and the DMV site warms up your recall before sitting down.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: Who should customers with disabilities or special needs notify when they need application or testing assistance?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Letting counter staff at any branch know early ensures accessible accommodations are set up smoothly.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: How many knowledge attempts are allowed per business day, and when are personal translators barred?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Because Virginia offers audio playback, ASL, and many translated screens, outside translators are prohibited wherever offered versions exist.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: Why do Virginia's audio, ASL, and multilingual computer versions eliminate using a translator?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Standardized built-in translations and audio keep testing fair and block human translators whenever a supported language exists.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: Which four forms of assistance, content sharing, or phone use are strictly banned during testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Pulling out a cell phone, trading items, or helping a neighbor invalidates your session on the spot.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: How does Virginia treat giving versus receiving help, and hunting items beforehand versus sharing them afterward?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Integrity rules cover both directions—getting or giving help during the session and hunting or leaking items outside it.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: How long must an applicant younger than eighteen wait after failing the knowledge exam—for example after failing January 1?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Notice how full days count—failing January 1 means fifteen full days pass before January 17 opens.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: What educational requirement kicks in if you fail the Virginia knowledge exam three times?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: After strike three, DMV locks out attempt four until you complete and pass classroom driver education.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: Instead of full classroom driver ed, what shorter course option can applicants eighteen or older use after three failures?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Adults eighteen and up can take an approved eight-hour manual course online or at school after failing thrice, then show DMV the certificate.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: Under what prior condition may an applicant younger than eighteen take the eight-hour manual course?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Minors cannot use the eight-hour manual course as a shortcut—they must show their classroom driver-ed certificate to the school first.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: How do Virginia's under-eighteen retake wait and post-third-failure course rules work for minors versus adults?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Minors wait fifteen full days per miss, and three misses require post-failure coursework—direct eight-hour option for adults, classroom-first for minors.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: After three knowledge failures, how does access to the eight-hour manual course differ for adults versus minors?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Adults jump straight into the eight-hour manual course, whereas minors qualify only if classroom driver ed is already done.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: Valid licenses from which U.S. states or five international jurisdictions waive Virginia's road skills check?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Spot the extra jurisdiction over the written waiver—Taiwan joins U.S. states, Canada, Germany, France, and South Korea for road waivers.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: Who provides the road-check car, which vehicle type is banned, and what tags and safety gear must work?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Bring your own registered, inspected four-wheel car—never an autocycle—with working brakes, belts, lights, horn, mirrors, signals, and speedometer.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Which two alternative forms prove your readiness before the road examiner lets you start?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Hand the examiner either an accepted driver-ed completion certificate or form CSMA 19 signed by a licensed supervisor.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: Can you take Virginia's road skills check without either a driver-ed certificate or form CSMA 19?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Showing up without either your school completion certificate or a completed CSMA 19 checklist cancels your road drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: Where do applicants younger than eighteen take their road skills check, and what guides home-schooled teens?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Teens under eighteen complete road skills inside public, private, or commercial driver ed, while home-schoolers follow sheet HS 3.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: At age eighteen or older, what two tracks unlock your first road check, and who administers each?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Adults either hold a learner permit sixty days for DMV road testing or complete approved driver ed for school road testing.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: How do road-check options differ between applicants under eighteen and applicants eighteen or older?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Under-eighteen applicants test through their driver-ed course, whereas adults pick between a sixty-day permit with DMV or school driver ed.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: What daily cap, single-failure wait, and three-failure requirement govern DMV road skills attempts?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: You get one try per business day, a two-day wait per miss, and mandatory post-third-failure behind-the-wheel school before try four.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How does the consequence of one DMV road-check failure compare with a third DMV failure?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Missing once or twice only costs a two-day breather, whereas strike three requires passing approved behind-the-wheel training.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: What happens during DMV vision screening, and what happens if you do not pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Counter screening checks letter and number acuity rather than full eye health, referring failed readings to an eye specialist.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: What license code applies if you need glasses or contacts to pass, and how can laser surgery remove it?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Corrective lenses add code C, which lifts post-surgery once you pass unaided at DMV or submit form MED 4.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: What puts the C restriction onto a Virginia license, and what two ways clear it after laser correction?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Never stop wearing lenses under code C until DMV records either a fresh unaided machine pass or form MED 4.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: What visual acuity and horizontal field of vision are required for an unrestricted Virginia license?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Hitting twenty-forty and a hundred-ten-degree horizontal span in one or both eyes unlocks full day-and-night driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: What acuity and horizontal field—including single-eye nose and temple angles—qualify for daylight-only driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Daylight-only licenses need twenty-seventy acuity and seventy horizontal degrees—or thirty nasal and forty temporal in a single eye.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How do acuity and horizontal field numbers compare between unrestricted and daylight-only licenses?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Daylight-only remembers easily as double-seventy—twenty-seventy and seventy degrees—versus twenty-forty and one-ten unrestricted.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: Between which exact sunrise and sunset buffers may a daylight-only license holder drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Twilight glare and dim shadows are excluded—wait thirty minutes past sunrise and park thirty minutes before sunset.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: What driving rules attach to a C restriction versus a daylight-only restriction?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Code C requires corrective lenses on every trip, while daylight-only trims thirty minutes off both ends of sun hours.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: Which DMV publication covers licensing rules for drivers who wear bioptic telescopic lenses?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: Special telescopic-lens qualifications and rules are detailed inside DMV publication MED 44.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: How does DMV form MED 4 differ in purpose from DMV publication MED 44?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: Eye doctors file single-digit MED 4 to report vision results, while double-four MED 44 explains bioptic lens licensing.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: Is cutting across a parking lot to skip a red light legal, and whose command overrides every sign or light?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Ducking through corner gas stations or fields to dodge controls is illegal, and a live police officer outranks every display.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: Which five groups of road users are legally bound by Virginia traffic signals?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Every traveler sharing the street—whether on four wheels, two wheels, or two feet—follows intersection lights.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: Where must your vehicle stop at a steady red light when a stop line is painted versus when none exists?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Creeping onto the crosswalk forces pedestrians into live cross traffic while you wait for green.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: What stop, scan, and yield steps are required before turning right on a steady red light?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: After halting completely, check both directions and yield to walkers, cars, motorcycles, bicycles, and mopeds.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: Which two intersection controls forbid making a right turn on red?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Either a No Turn on Red plaque or a lit rightward red arrow holds you stopped until green.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: Between which street types—and under what conditions—is a left turn on red legal in Virginia?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Turning left on red from or onto a two-way street crosses opposing lanes and is always illegal.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: How do the street requirements and bans compare for turning right on red versus left on red?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Both demand a full stop, yield, and no prohibiting plaque or red arrow, while left on red adds one-way-to-one-way streets.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: What does a steady red arrow command in Virginia, and what sole exception allows turning?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Virginia bans turning through any steady red arrow unless an explicit Right or Left on Red Arrow After Stop plaque stands there.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: Why shouldn't you assume Virginia's red-light and red-arrow turn rules apply when driving out of state?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Some jurisdictions ban turns on red citywide or treat red arrows differently, so check local rules when traveling.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: How do you handle a flashing red intersection light, and what rule applies at a railroad flashing red?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Treat intersection flashing red like a stop sign, and never roll railroad flashing reds even if tracks look empty.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: What three steps let you proceed in the direction of a flashing red arrow?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Unlike a steady red arrow that holds you waiting, a flashing red arrow works like a directional stop-and-yield.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: How does a steady red arrow differ from a flashing red arrow in Virginia?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Steady red arrows lock you in place absent a special plaque, whereas flashing red arrows release you after stopping and yielding.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: How does a steady circular red light differ from a flashing red light for straight-through traffic?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Straight-through drivers wait out the entire steady red cycle, whereas flashing red lets you proceed once cross traffic clears.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: What must you do at a steady yellow light or arrow depending on whether you can stop safely?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Halt before entering whenever safe; if already inside or too close to brake safely, clear cautiously without flooring it.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: What road condition and driving response belong to a flashing yellow light?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Flashing amber spotlights extra-risky crossings or curves where easing speed keeps you ready for surprises.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: How does your response to a steady yellow display differ from a flashing yellow display?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Steady yellow signals an imminent red stop, whereas flashing yellow asks for slower cautious travel without stopping.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: What separates a flashing red light from a flashing yellow light at an intersection?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Cross streets often split the pair—flashing red must stop and yield while flashing yellow slows without stopping.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: How do you complete a turn under a flashing yellow arrow, and whom must you scan for?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Opposing green traffic—especially slim motorcycles, bikes, and mopeds—plus pedestrians own the right-of-way before you turn.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: Even with a green light or green arrow, when may you move, and who yields on an unprotected green turn?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: Never nose into a blocked box or cut off straggling walkers, and always yield to oncoming traffic on plain green turns.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: How does turning on an ordinary circular green light differ from turning on a green arrow?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: A directional green arrow holds opposing traffic, whereas a plain green ball leaves you yielding to oncoming cars and walkers.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: How do you cross when traffic lights are completely dark, and what two situations override that rule?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Power outages turn uncontrolled intersections dangerous unless temporary stop signs stand there or law enforcement waves cars through.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: What rule applies to a travel lane marked overhead with a steady red X?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Reversible lanes under a red X often carry head-on opposing traffic or closed emergency zones.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: What must you do when an overhead lane gantry shows a yellow X or yellow diagonal downward arrow?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Yellow overhead lane warnings mean a red X closure is coming soon, so merge safely out of that lane.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: What does an overhead green downward arrow allow compared with a one-way or two-way turn arrow?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: Downward green arrows open normal through travel, whereas overhead turn symbols restrict entry strictly to turning.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: How do overhead red X, yellow X, and green arrow lane displays compare?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Reversible highway corridors switch smoothly when drivers read red as closed, yellow as vacating, and green as open.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: Through what four light stages does a Virginia pedestrian hybrid beacon step once triggered?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: Drivers get flashing then solid yellow warnings, hold on solid double red for walkers, then proceed cautiously on clear alternating red.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: On a pedestrian hybrid beacon, how do solid double reds differ from alternating flashing reds?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Stay planted during solid double red while pedestrians cross, then treat clear alternating wigwag reds as stop-and-proceed with caution.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: How do sign shapes and colors help drivers in thick fog or from long distances?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Long before lettering sharpens into focus—or when fog blurs words—distinct silhouettes and background colors telegraph the rule.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: What meanings belong to red-and-white, black-and-white, standard yellow, and fluorescent yellow-green signs?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: Red commands stops or bans, black posts laws, yellow warns of hazards, and bright yellow-green highlights school, walker, and bike zones.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: What quick meaning belongs to black-with-white, yellow-with-black, and red-with-white signs?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Sorting regulatory black, warning yellow, and prohibitive red gives instant comprehension on unfamiliar roads.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: What does each background color—green, blue, brown, orange, and fluorescent pink—tell Virginia drivers?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: Virginia tests pink specifically—fluorescent pink flags emergency traffic incidents while orange marks construction, green directions, blue services, and brown history.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.question_text: How does an orange-and-black warning sign differ from a fluorescent pink-and-black warning sign?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.teaching_text: Planned roadwork wears orange, whereas unplanned crashes, hazardous spills, or emergency scenes put up fluorescent pink.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: Where must you halt at an eight-sided stop octagon, and who yields if two cars arrive together at an all-way stop?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: Stop completely at the post, line, crosswalk, or curb, and on simultaneous all-way arrivals the driver on the left yields.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: What three steps does a triangular yield sign require as you approach?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Ease off the gas early and stand ready to brake so vehicles, walkers, and cyclists pass unhurried.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: How does the stopping requirement of an octagon compare with a yield triangle?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Never treat an octagon like a yield—every octagon requires dead-zero wheels, while triangles stop only for conflicting traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: How do vertical rectangular signs differ in purpose from horizontal rectangular signs?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Standing tall signals enforceable rules like speed limits, whereas wide horizontal boards point out routes and directions.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: Which rectangle orientation posts legal instructions, and which gives directional information?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Spot the rectangle's posture early so you never mistake a mandatory lane command for a casual route guide.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: What do diamond-shaped signs warn about, and what three responses should follow?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Seeing a diamond tells you special road conditions lie ahead—ease speed, sharpen focus, and stay ready to brake.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: Which two school areas use five-sided pentagon signs, and how can a second pentagon clarify location?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: An advance pentagon alerts you entering the school zone while a follow-up pentagon pinpoints the exact student crosswalk.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: What force do regulatory signs carry, and how do you read a red circle with a diagonal slash?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Universal red-slash graphics forbid whatever maneuver or vehicle appears inside the ring, no language needed.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: Under what weather does a posted speed limit apply, and can you get ticketed driving at or below it?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Posted numbers assume dry clear pavement—driving the limit through rain, snow, or ice can still earn an unsafe-speed ticket.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: How do standard metal speed-limit signs differ from overhead electronic speed displays?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Electronic highway boards drop legal speeds dynamically during congestion, fog, or storms.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: What is happening if you face Do Not Enter or Wrong Way plaques, and what three moves must you make?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Opposing traffic is coming straight toward your bumper—brake immediately, get onto the edge, and turn around carefully.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: What traffic rule does a One Way plaque state?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Checking One Way arrows before turning onto city cross streets prevents turning head-on into single-direction lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: How does the message of Do Not Enter and Wrong Way differ from a One Way plaque?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: One Way simply guides legal street direction, whereas Do Not Enter and Wrong Way warn you've already aimed backward.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: Why does a posted No Left Turn plaque also make U-turns illegal in Virginia?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: This is a classic Virginia test favorite—because a U-turn equals two left turns here, No Left Turn bans both.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: What do No Right Turn, No U-Turn, and No Turn on Red plaques forbid, and when do you go under No Turn on Red?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Each plaque outlaws its exact turn, and No Turn on Red keeps you planted behind the line until green.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: In Virginia, how does the scope of No Left Turn differ from No U-Turn?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Under a No U-Turn plaque you can still make a standard ninety-degree left turn, whereas No Left Turn blocks both.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: What must you do past a Do Not Pass plaque even if the oncoming lane looks empty?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Hidden dips, curves, or side roads justify passing bans even when your quick glance forward looks wide open.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: What does a Left Turn Yield on Green plaque remind left-turning drivers at a green light?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: A circular green never grants turn priority—halt in position, let opposing traffic clear, and turn cautiously.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: How does No Turn on Red differ in timing from Left Turn Yield on Green?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: One governs red-phase waiting while the other governs yielding to opposing cars during an active green ball.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: What physical obstacle ahead does a Keep Right sign warn of, and where do you steer?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Raised medians, islands, and bridge piers split the road ahead, so stay cleanly to the side the arrow points.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: What do Lane Use Control plaques require of vehicles traveling inside that marked lane?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Going straight out of a mandatory turn-only lane sideswipes neighboring drivers making permitted dual turns.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: How do Lane Use Control arrows differ in purpose from a Keep Right divider arrow?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Lane-use panels lock in intersection turn maneuvers, while Keep Right simply guides your tires past a raised divider.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: Which two vehicle categories may legally travel in lanes marked with High Occupancy Vehicle plaques?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Solo drivers earn hefty HOV tickets during restricted hours unless riding a bus or carrying the posted passenger minimum.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: Who is permitted to park in stalls marked by Disabled Parking plaques?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Accessible stalls stay reserved strictly for vehicles authorized by valid disabled parking permits or plates.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: What should you do as soon as you spot a roadside warning sign?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Warning diamonds buy advance reaction time so you slow early and spot upcoming markings, controls, or work zones.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: How does a highway exit advisory speed plaque differ from a Reduced Speed Limit Ahead warning?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Yellow exit tabs recommend the safe ramp curve speed, whereas Reduced Speed Limit Ahead warns a lower legal limit starts soon.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: Which speed warning recommends safe exit-ramp speed, and which announces an upcoming legal speed-limit drop?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Ease off the highway pace early on both—tight ramp curves punish speeders physically and dropped limits ticket them legally.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: What do Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead, and Signal Ahead diamonds tell you to do?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Blind hills or curves often hide the intersection itself, so start shedding speed before the control comes into view.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: What zone begins at a No Passing Zone pennant, and what must you do?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Mounted on the left side where passers peek out, the pennant tells you to stay tucked in lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: At a Merge warning diamond, which lane bears legal responsibility for blending safely?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Virginia splits merge responsibility across both streams—neither lane owns the right to bully or block the other.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: Under a lane-reduction warning where the right lane ends, what is expected of right-lane and left-lane drivers?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Right-lane drivers look for an open gap to move left while through-lane drivers cooperate smoothly to let them in.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: How does lane responsibility at a Merge diamond differ from a right-lane-ends reduction diamond?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: True merges join two equal streams together, whereas a lane drop ends the right lane into the continuing left lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: What roadway changes do Divided Highway Begins and Divided Highway Ends warn of, and which side do you keep?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Both diamonds show a median nose—stay right whether entering separated one-way carriageways or returning to undivided two-way pavement.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: How does Divided Highway Begins differ in traffic layout from Divided Highway Ends?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Watch where the black median island sits on the diamond—ahead at the top means splitting, behind at the bottom means rejoining.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: What three driving adjustments belong wherever a Slippery When Wet diamond stands?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Rain mixes with pavement oil into a slick film where hard braking or sharp steering triggers instant hydroplaning or skids.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: Which vehicles are barred from continuing under an overpass marked with a low clearance diamond?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Box trucks, RVs, or rooftop cargo exceeding the posted feet-and-inches figure will wedge violently into bridge beams.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: What specific precaution pairs with a steep-hill diamond versus a leaping-deer crossing diamond?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Test your brakes before descending steep grades, and drop speed while scanning roadsides through active deer corridors.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: How must you pass horse-drawn buggies—including horn and distance rules—and how do you pass farm equipment?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Honking spooks horses into traffic—slow quietly and give buggies at least three feet, and slow or stop behind wide tractors until clear.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.question_text: Which two specific rules apply when passing a horse-drawn buggy beyond standard slow-and-clear farm-equipment passing?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.teaching_text: Live horses startle unlike steel farm machinery, adding the strict horn ban and three-foot clearance rule.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: What do pedestrian crossing versus bicycle crossing diamonds tell you, and what can a companion arrow plaque add?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Expect walkers stepping out and cyclists crossing or riding alongside, watching for supplemental downward arrows pinpointing the exact crossing.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: What four duties apply at school zone and school crossing pentagons?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Scan actively for children, prepare to slow or halt, obey school speed limits, and follow crossing guards at arrow-marked crosswalks.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: How do the manual's instructions compare across pedestrian crossings, bicycle crossings, and school zones or crossings?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Pedestrian signs stress slowing and stop-readiness, bike signs stress careful driving, and school pentagons add speed limits and crossing guards.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: Why must drivers reduce speed when approaching open joints on Virginia bridges or ramps?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Sudden metal gaps can destabilize two-wheeled balance ahead of you, making smooth speed reductions critical behind riders.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: What two hazards do lane-spanning expansion joints create, especially during rain?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Slick metal seams across bridge decks break tire grip instantly if you brake hard or steer abruptly over them.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: What road change does an intersection warning sign signal, and how should you respond?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Cross-traffic pulling out unexpectedly from hidden side approaches is a classic rural crash setup unless your eyes are scanning early.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: How do the required driver actions at a Y intersection compare with those at a T intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Exam questions test whether your road merely splits forward or terminates completely at a mandatory stop-and-yield crossroad.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: Which junction only splits your forward path, and which terminates your road with a stop and yield?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Confusing a dead-end T crossroad for a flowing Y split risks blowing straight past a stop sign into cross traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: Who holds right-of-way at a roundabout entrance, and which direction does traffic circulate around the center island?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Drivers already circling the island always hold priority, and turning left directly at entry puts you head-on against flow.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: What dual geometry does a right-curve-with-side-road warning describe?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Sightlines tighten mid-bend right where side-street drivers pull out from your left, leaving zero margin for excess speed.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: How does Virginia distinguish sharp-turn warnings from standard right-then-left curve warnings?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Abrupt ninety-degree-style bends punish late braking far harder than sweeping reverse curves unless you set entry speed early.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: How should you respond to a curve paired with a safe speed plaque versus a winding road sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Shedding speed before the first apex and keeping pace down through every linked bend prevents drifting across the centerline.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: What separates single or double sharp-turn signs from a winding road warning?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Knowing whether recovery comes after one or two corners versus a continuous chain keeps you from accelerating too soon.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: What specific danger does a low-ground-clearance railroad crossing sign highlight?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Trailers and low-slung cars can bottom out dead-center across live rails where raised track beds drop off sharply.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: How does the danger of a low-ground rail crossing contrast with bridge open and expansion joints?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Permit exams pair similar surface warnings to test whether the threat is stranding an undercarriage or losing wet tire grip.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: Which four actions do advance railroad crossing signs call for as you approach?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Freight trains take over a mile to stop, so every crossing defense relies on drivers preparing well upstream.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: What does a railroad crossbuck mark, and why is scanning one direction never enough?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Trains run unscheduled from both directions and on parallel rails, turning a single-glance roll-through into a fatal trap.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: How do upstream advance crossing signs and trackside crossbucks divide the warning job?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Missing the early round sign leaves too little braking room once the white X appears right beside the steel.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: When red lights start flashing at a crossbuck, how long must you hold your stop and what hidden threat lurks?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Pulling forward the instant a caboose clears can put you straight into a second train hidden on the adjacent track.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: What extra danger do multiple-track crossings add beyond a single-track rail line?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: One passing train blocks your view and sound of another locomotive closing fast from the opposite direction.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: How must you handle a gated railroad crossing from the moment lights flash until the arms clear?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Weaving around lowered arms is both illegal and deadly because fast trains arrive far sooner than eyes judge.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: How does your legal duty escalate from a bare crossbuck to flashing lights to lowered gates?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Test questions check that passive signs demand yield readiness while active lights and arms lock in mandatory stops.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: What white pavement legend may be painted directly on your lane ahead of railroad tracks?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Pavement legends reinforce roadside signs right in your sightline when trees or trucks block shoulder posts.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: What space check must pass before your front bumper ever rolls onto railroad tracks?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Queueing behind stopped traffic with your rear bumper hanging over the rails leaves zero escape if flashers start.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: If your engine dies on railroad tracks, how should everyone evacuate and in which direction should you run?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Running forty-five degrees away toward the approaching locomotive keeps flying wreckage pushed forward instead of into your back.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: What rule keeps a moving car safe at tracks, and what replaces it if the car stalls there?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Smart drivers never trap themselves in queues, and smart survivors never waste seconds cranking a dead starter on steel.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: When are school buses required to stop at railroad crossings in Virginia?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Trailing too closely behind a school bus near rails causes rear-end collisions when the driver makes that mandatory stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: How do you alert the railroad if you spot a hazard or blocked track at a crossing?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Dispatchers use that exact posted crossing code to halt or reroute approaching locomotives before impact.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.question_text: What rule governs school buses at dark crossings, and how are track hazards reported?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.teaching_text: Expecting every yellow bus to halt and knowing where to find the railroad's direct line prevents multi-casualty rail crashes.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: What does orange signage signal in work zones, and what fines hit speeding versus handheld phone use there?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: Workers stand inches from live lanes behind thin cones, so Virginia backs orange zones with steep court penalties.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: How does Virginia's maximum work-zone speeding fine compare with the handheld device fine?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: DMV distractors love swapping these two dollar figures, so keep speeding at double the flat phone penalty.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: Which road conditions do rough road, bump, and uneven lane signs warn about, and who faces extra risk?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Scarified asphalt lips and loose aggregate can grab a narrow front tire, making extra following space vital behind motorcycles.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: What shift in driving conditions do road construction and detour signs announce?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Shifted lanes, sudden tapers, and heavy trucks entering traffic punish drivers cruising on muscle memory.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: What two jobs do large flashing arrow boards and electronic message signs perform in work zones?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Merging early when high-mounted arrows appear avoids last-second squeeze plays right at the cone taper.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.question_text: What enforcement awaits drivers where a photo speed enforcement sign stands in a work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.teaching_text: Even when no patrol cruiser is parked near the cones, roadside sensors log plate numbers above the posted limit.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: How do arrow boards, human flaggers, and photo signs split traffic control duties in a work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: Recognizing whether a device shifts your lane, commands an immediate stop, or enforces speed keeps work-zone passes clean.
sec04-card-sec04-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Arrows merge, flaggers direct, cameras ticket

visual_sync.text_span: Arrows merge, flaggers direct, cameras ticket

sec04-card-sec04-F25.question_text: How should you position your vehicle and manage lane changes inside and right past work-zone drums or barriers?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.teaching_text: Darting sideways before clearing the final cone risks clipping hidden crew trucks or merging traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.question_text: What discipline applies between work-zone channelizing devices, and what rule holds as you exit the zone?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.teaching_text: Maintaining steady lane discipline past the last drum prevents sideswipes where narrow chutes reopen to highway width.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: How should you sit in the driver's seat, where on the clock do your hands belong, and how should you grip the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Lowering hands below the airbag deployment path prevents severe arm or facial injuries if a front crash inflates the bag.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: Which steering posture and clock positions does Virginia teach, and which part of the hand should stay off the grip?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Wrapping fingers and thumbs lightly around the lower rim gives crisp steering feedback without locking tense wrists.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: What personal obligation do you take on every time you sit behind the wheel in Virginia?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Every choice on speed, space, and signaling ripples directly onto passengers, pedestrians, and neighboring motorists.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: What weather and roadway assumption is built into every posted speed limit sign?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Driving the full posted number through pouring rain, fog, or glare can still earn an unsafe-speed citation or cause a wreck.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: What action is mandatory whenever signs indicate an active school-zone or work-zone speed restriction?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Children near crosswalks and road crews beside live lanes leave zero room for highway-speed stopping distances.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: Should you read a speed limit sign as a guaranteed safe pace anytime or an ideal-condition upper bound?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Exam questions love testing that posted numbers cap clear-day travel rather than promising safety on slick or crowded pavement.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: Which roadside zones and environmental hazards require dropping below a road's normal posted limit?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Adapting pace downward whenever rain, roadwork, or school flashers shrink your safety cushion keeps traction and sightlines intact.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: When no speed sign is posted, what three default limits govern Virginia cars and motorcycles by area?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Memorizing twenty-five in town, thirty-five on gravel, and fifty-five on open roads nails one of Virginia's classic exam staples.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: How do Virginia's unsigned speed caps for cars and motorcycles step up from neighborhoods to gravel to open highways?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Any posted regulatory plaque overrides these statutory baselines, so scan the roadside whenever town streets meet rural routes.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: Why can driving at the exact posted speed limit still be unlawful or dangerous?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Active zone flashers, torn-up construction lanes, and slick storms all erase the ideal baseline that the sign was built around.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What effect do active school or work-zone plaques, roadwork, and bad weather share on your speed?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Whether a flashing school beacon or a sudden downpour triggers it, shedding speed restores braking margin before trouble starts.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: Which two broad triggers force you below a highway's standard posted speed?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Both legal zone schedules and physical traction loss require backing off the throttle right away.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: Under what condition is driving slower than the posted maximum legal in Virginia?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Crawling needlessly far below highway pace creates dangerous closing-speed differentials and triggers impeded-traffic citations.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: Where does Virginia draw the legal line on choosing to drive below the speed limit?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Drivers may ease off comfortably so long as they are not bottlenecking healthy traffic behind them.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Which three sequential factors combine to create your total stopping distance?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Your car covers huge ground while your eyes spot danger and your foot moves, well before brake pads ever bite.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: How severely can wet pavement stretch your vehicle's braking distance?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Water lubricating asphalt cuts tire friction in half, turning a routine dry-day gap into a rear-end collision.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What three components make up total stopping distance, and how does rain alter the final phase?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Even alert eyes and quick feet cannot rescue you on wet roads if your following gap ignores doubled skidding distance.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: Which roadside sign and two red signal displays always command a complete stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Rolling through an octagon, solid red lens, or flashing red beacon is an instant road-test fail and intersection hazard.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: What do flashing red lights and an extended stop arm on a loading school bus command?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Students dart unpredictably around the front bumper and across lanes whenever a yellow bus opens its doors.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: Who must stop for a loading school bus even if its signals are off, and what sole roadway feature frees opposing lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Painted center turn lanes never count as barriers, so opposing drivers must still halt unless a raised median or divider separates roadways.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: When does oncoming traffic have to stop for a school bus's red lights, and when may the far side proceed?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Even when a physical median lets opposing lanes roll past, stay vigilant for kids running unexpectedly near the crossing.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: Without a posted speed sign, how fast may cars and motorcycles travel in school, business, and residential zones?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Dense foot traffic, parked cars, and driveways pack town streets, making twenty-five miles per hour the life-saving default.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: What unsigned speed ceiling governs Virginia school, business, and residential districts, and what overrides it?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Assume twenty-five miles per hour across every neighborhood or commercial block unless a regulatory sign states another number.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: How much does wearing a seat belt improve your odds of surviving a crash and avoiding severe injury?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Staying strapped inside the vehicle's steel safety cage keeps you from being thrown onto pavement or crushed in rollovers.
sec12-card-sec12-F01.must_match_memory_hook: Doubles survival, more than doubles injury-escape

visual_sync.text_span: Doubles survival, more than doubles injury-escape

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: Which seating positions require seat belts in Virginia, and what legal responsibility falls on the driver for passengers under eighteen?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Adult back-seat passengers are no longer exempt in Virginia, and the driver takes responsibility for securing every rider under eighteen.
sec12-card-sec12-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Every seat belted; driver secures under-eighteens

visual_sync.text_span: Every seat belted; driver secures under-eighteens

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Where must the lap and shoulder straps sit on your body, including the rule for expectant mothers?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Tucking a shoulder strap under your arm or riding a lap belt high over your stomach causes severe internal crash injuries.
sec12-card-sec12-F03.must_match_memory_hook: Low over thighs, snug across chest

visual_sync.text_span: Low over thighs, snug across chest

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: What strap shortcuts must you never take, and where should a pregnant occupant position the lap strap?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Strong hip and shoulder bones absorb crash forces safely, whereas soft abdominal tissue cannot.
sec12-card-sec12-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Never under arm; lowest on pelvis

visual_sync.text_span: Never under arm; lowest on pelvis

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: Who has authority to excuse someone from wearing a seat belt, and what must that person carry in the vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Verbal excuses never count at a traffic stop—the exempted rider must carry the doctor's signed note naming them and the condition.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: How universal is Virginia's seat-belt mandate across the cabin, and what single exception exists?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: From front buckets to third-row benches, every occupant buckles up unless holding a signed medical exemption from a physician.
sec12-card-sec12-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Everyone buckles unless carrying physician waiver

visual_sync.text_span: Everyone buckles unless carrying physician waiver

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: When police signal you to pull over, what parking, lighting, engine, audio, and window steps should you take right away?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Switching on your cabin dome light at night and shutting off the engine and stereo immediately signals cooperation and lowers tension.
sec12-card-sec12-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Safe stop, hazards, dome, engine off

visual_sync.text_span: Safe stop, hazards, dome, engine off

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: While waiting during a traffic stop, what must you and your passengers do with seat belts, hands, and sudden movements?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Unbuckling or diving toward a console as an officer walks up looks like hiding contraband or reaching for a weapon.
sec12-card-sec12-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Stay buckled, hands visible, zero reaching

visual_sync.text_span: Stay buckled, hands visible, zero reaching

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: How do your initial vehicle-setup actions at a traffic stop transition into how everyone sits while the officer approaches?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Once flashers, dome light, window, and ignition are set, keeping belts clicked and hands in plain view keeps everyone safe.
sec12-card-sec12-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Secure cabin first, then hold still

visual_sync.text_span: Secure cabin first, then hold still

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: How should you reach for your license, registration, and insurance when asked, and when may you ask to see officer ID?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Telling the officer where your wallet or registration sits before moving one hand prevents misunderstandings, and unmarked stops permit ID checks.
sec12-card-sec12-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Announce spot, one hand wheeled, verify

visual_sync.text_span: Announce spot, one hand wheeled, verify

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: Where do ticket disputes belong, what does signing a citation actually mean, and what happens if you refuse to sign?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Your signature merely acknowledges receipt and promises to respond—refusing to sign can turn a routine ticket into an arrest.
sec12-card-sec12-F08.must_match_memory_hook: Sign without guilt, contest in court

visual_sync.text_span: Sign without guilt, contest in court

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: What three rules govern retrieving your papers, verifying a plainclothes or unmarked stop, and signing a handed ticket?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Combining calm, announced movements with signing the summons keeps a roadside stop routine while preserving every courtroom defense.
sec12-card-sec12-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Slow announced reach, check ID, sign

visual_sync.text_span: Slow announced reach, check ID, sign

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: Which side of your car may an officer walk up to, and why is arguing at the roadside pointless?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Officers often approach the passenger window to stay clear of fast highway lanes, and only a judge can dismiss citations.
sec12-card-sec12-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Either side approach; court settles disputes

visual_sync.text_span: Either side approach; court settles disputes

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: What medical note can excuse a child restraint, and what fines apply to first versus repeat child-restraint violations?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Without a carried physician statement naming the child and medical grounds, repeat restraint violations jump tenfold to five hundred dollars.
sec12-card-sec12-F09.must_match_memory_hook: Carry physician waiver; fifty then five-hundred

visual_sync.text_span: Carry physician waiver; fifty then five-hundred

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: Who must carry a child's medical restraint waiver, what reasons qualify, and how steep is a second violation?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Weight, physical fitness, or medical exceptions only count when the driver carries the signed statement naming that child.
sec12-card-sec12-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Driver carries waiver; repeat hits five-hundred

visual_sync.text_span: Driver carries waiver; repeat hits five-hundred

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: Where is the safest seat in the car for children, why must you never hold a child on your lap, and how should doors be set?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Center-back gives maximum buffer from side impacts, while lap-held children get crushed between the adult's body and dashboard in crashes.
sec12-card-sec12-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Center rear seat, never on laps

visual_sync.text_span: Center rear seat, never on laps

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: Which cargo areas are off-limits to children, and under what age is riding in a pickup truck bed illegal?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Even bolting a camper shell onto a pickup bed does not make it legal or crash-safe for riders under sixteen.
sec12-card-sec12-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Skip cargo bays and pickup beds

visual_sync.text_span: Skip cargo bays and pickup beds

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: Why are adult laps, station-wagon cargo bays, open hatchbacks, and pickup beds all barred for young passengers?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Unbelted cargo spaces and adult laps offer zero crash-tested restraint and expose kids to carbon monoxide or ejection.
sec12-card-sec12-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Zero restraint zones crush or eject

visual_sync.text_span: Zero restraint zones crush or eject

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: How do child door-lock habits pair with center-rear installation and local inspection events?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Free community check events catch loose harness straps, while child locks stop curious toddlers from popping doors in motion.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: What safety equipment must pair with airbags, and which body parts do frontal airbags shield?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Airbags are supplemental cushions designed around belted riders—without a seat belt, you slam into an inflating bag out of position.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: How far should you sit from the steering wheel, where should a tilt wheel aim, and where belong riders twelve and under?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Sitting closer than ten inches puts your face inside the airbag's explosive deployment zone, and front bags endanger kids twelve and under.
sec12-card-sec12-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Ten inches back, kids ride rear

visual_sync.text_span: Ten inches back, kids ride rear

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: Which four habits let airbags cushion occupants instead of injuring them?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Every Virginia airbag test item boils down to belting up, ten-inch wheel clearance, chest-aimed tilt, and keeping twelve-and-unders in back.
sec12-card-sec12-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Buckle, ten inches, tilt, kids rear

visual_sync.text_span: Buckle, ten inches, tilt, kids rear

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: Through what ages must children ride rear-facing and in child seats or boosters, and when is front-seat placement allowed?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Toddlers stay rear-facing until age two or the seat's upper limit, and front placement requires no rear seat plus no active airbag.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: Which seven posture and strap checks must a child pass before graduating from a booster to an adult seat belt?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: If knees cannot bend naturally at the seat edge with spine flat and feet planted the whole trip, keep the booster.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: How does a growing child step safely from infant carrier to forward harness, booster, and finally adult belts?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Rushing a child into adult belts early lets straps ride up onto the neck and soft belly during sudden stops.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: Under what exact two conditions may a rear-facing child seat go in front, and where are kids twelve and younger safer?
