sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: How do you reinstate a suspended Virginia license, and when must you retake vision, knowledge, and road checks?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Temporary suspensions normally clear once fees and legal-presence documents are filed, unless your plastic license sat expired over a year.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: What does revocation do to your driving privilege, and what steps are required once the revocation term ends?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Unlike a temporary hold, revocation wipes your credential off the books so you start from scratch with full testing and fees.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: How does getting your license back after a suspension compare with starting over after a revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Standard suspensions restore with fees and legal-presence paperwork, whereas every revocation forces a brand-new application and all three screenings.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: Which serious DUI, crash, fraud, felony, or police-evasion offenses force Virginia courts or DMV to suspend or revoke?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Zero discretion exists when impaired driving, fatal wrecks, interlock dodging, DMV lies, test stand-ins, drug crimes, or fleeing police happen.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: Which two serious moving-violation convictions give a Virginia court discretion to suspend or revoke your license?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Judges weigh how dangerous the driving was and can bench your privilege for either reckless or aggressive driving.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: How do mandatory suspension offenses like DUI or exam impersonation differ from reckless or aggressive driving?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: DMV questions love blending mandatory and discretionary lists—impaired driving, felonies, manslaughter, and stand-ins mandate loss, whereas reckless stays optional.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: Which three unlicensed, suspended-driving, or post-charge testing offenses also sit on the discretionary suspension list?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Driving without a valid license, ignoring a non-DUI suspension, or refusing blood or breath testing under a DUI charge invites suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: What three demerit-point values does Virginia DMV assign to traffic convictions, and over which two time windows?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Every Virginia court conviction lands on your DMV record as three, four, or six demerits tracked across rolling one- and two-year spans.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: How do unlicensed driving and breath-refusal cases differ from routine moving violations in DMV tracking?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Unlicensed driving and test refusal expose you directly to discretionary suspension, whereas everyday citations build toward clinic and suspension point totals.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: What happens to a driver younger than eighteen after a first, second, and third demerit or seat-belt conviction?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Strike one orders a ninety-day clinic deadline, strike two suspends ninety days, and strike three revokes one year or until eighteen.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: What requirement triggers if an eighteen- or nineteen-year-old receives any demerit-point or seat-belt conviction?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Even after turning eighteen, Virginia keeps older teens on a one-ticket trigger that mandates completing a driver-improvement clinic.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: How does the three-conviction penalty ladder under age eighteen compare with the rule at ages eighteen and nineteen?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Drivers under eighteen climb from clinic to ninety-day suspension to year-long revocation, while eighteen- and nineteen-year-olds draw the clinic order.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: For drivers eighteen and older, which twelve- and twenty-four-month point totals trigger a clinic versus an immediate ninety-day suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Twelve in one year or eighteen in two gives ninety days for a clinic, whereas eighteen in one or twenty-four in two suspends immediately.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: How many adult demerit points separate the clinic-order threshold from the automatic ninety-day suspension threshold?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Notice the six-point gap—hitting twelve in a year or eighteen in two mandates coursework before automatic ninety-day suspension hits.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: Which four driver abilities does medical review evaluate, how can it finish, and what reinstatement proof does it waive?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: DMV checks consciousness, perception, judgment, and motor skills via doctors or retests—ending clean, restricted, monitored, or suspended without legal-presence re-proof.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: How does missing a mandatory clinic deadline differ in outcome from a DMV medical fitness review?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Skipping an ordered clinic locks in suspension until you finish, whereas medical review can clear, restrict, monitor periodically, or suspend.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: What insurance certification or dollar fee is required when registering a motor vehicle in Virginia?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Every Virginia vehicle registration forces you to either swear active liability coverage exists or pay the five-hundred-dollar uninsured-vehicle fee.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: How does Virginia's registration insurance requirement contrast with the reinstatement rule after a medical suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Tagging a car always requires active coverage or the five-hundred-dollar fee, whereas returning from medical review skips legal-presence documents.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: Which two insurance-related mistakes trigger a Virginia license and registration suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Failing to submit DMV-requested insurance verification or canceling your policy while keeping active license plates on the car suspends you.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: What delinquency time, dollar arrears, or legal noncompliance prompts child-support enforcement to suspend a license?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Falling ninety days or five thousand dollars behind on child support—or ignoring paternity and support warrants or subpoenas—suspends driving.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: How do Virginia's insurance suspension triggers differ from its child-support suspension triggers?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Insurance holds stem from unverified policies or unreturned plates, while support holds hit ninety-day or five-thousand-dollar arrears and dodged process.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: What testing agreement comes with driving Virginia roads, and what three-hour post-crash arrest rule applies?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Using Virginia roads agrees to probable-cause breath tests, and officers can arrest suspected crash DUIs anywhere within three hours warrant-free.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: What immediate administrative suspensions hit a first, second, and third breath refusal or point zero eight BAC—and how do multi-DUIs run?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Admin holds escalate from seven days to sixty days to held-until-trial before court penalties even add on, and multiple DUIs run consecutively.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: How do Virginia's three-hour implied-consent rule and the seven-sixty-trial administrative ladder work together?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: Implied consent reaches three hours post-wreck, and either refusing breath testing or blowing point zero eight triggers instant seven-, sixty-, or trial holds.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: Under what cabin-reach, container, and driver-appearance conditions can an open alcohol container trigger a drinking-while-operating charge?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Even an unlocked glovebox counts as passenger reach when a partly consumed drink pairs with driver signs of drinking.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: What mandatory extra jail, fine, and repeat community-service penalties stack onto a DUI with a passenger seventeen or younger?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: Endangering a rider seventeen or under tacks five mandatory jail days and five hundred to one thousand dollars onto base DUI—plus eighty repeat hours.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: How does Virginia's open-container rule compare with its DUI-with-a-minor-passenger enhancement?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: Partly empty containers within cabin reach plus drinking signs create an operating presumption, while DUI carrying youths seventeen-and-under stacks mandatory jail and fines.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: How long is the vehicle impounded for driving on an alcohol suspension versus repeat unlicensed driving?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Alcohol-suspended driving seizes the vehicle thirty days immediately plus up to ninety more on conviction, whereas repeat unlicensed driving holds up to three days.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: Up to how much can local Virginia ordinances bill a convicted DUI driver who triggers an emergency crash response?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Cities and counties can recover up to one thousand dollars directly from a DUI crasher for police, fire, and ambulance dispatch.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.question_text: How do Virginia's vehicle-impoundment timelines compare with local emergency-response billing in alcohol cases?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.teaching_text: Driving on an alcohol suspension locks up the car thirty plus ninety days, whereas causing an emergency DUI response adds a thousand-dollar local bill.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: What suspension, mandatory minimum fine, or community-service penalty hits an under-twenty-one driver at point zero two to under point zero eight BAC?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Even a single drink puts under-twenty-one drivers at point zero two—costing a year-long suspension plus five hundred dollars minimum or fifty service hours.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.question_text: How does an under-twenty-one conviction at point zero two BAC compare in length with a first adult administrative hold?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.teaching_text: Zero tolerance hits hard—an underage point-oh-two conviction strips driving for an entire year plus fine or service, dwarfing a seven-day first admin hold.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: What document must you physically carry every time you drive, and what three penalties can misuse bring?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Leaving your valid license or permit behind—or lending or misusing one—exposes you to fines, jail time, or license suspension.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: Where must a learner-permit supervisor sit, what normal age applies, and who qualifies at ages eighteen through twenty?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Your licensed, alert passenger rides shotgun at twenty-one-plus—dropping to eighteen through twenty strictly for legal guardians or full, half, or step siblings.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: How do cabin requirements differ between a fully licensed driver and a learner-permit holder?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Licensed drivers only need their valid card on them, whereas permit holders also need an alert twenty-one-plus—or eighteen-plus family—front-seat supervisor.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: At age nineteen or older, what two alternative milestones let you apply for a Virginia driver's license?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Applicants nineteen and up choose between holding a learner's permit for sixty days or finishing an approved driver-education course.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: How does the nineteen-plus applicant's permit-holding rule differ from the supervisor's age rule?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Don't scramble the numbers—nineteen-plus applicants wait sixty days or finish driver ed, while non-family front-seat supervisors must be twenty-one.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: What penalty tier can hit an underage driver convicted of driving after illegal drinking at point zero eight BAC or higher?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Crossing the adult intoxication threshold of point zero eight percent removes zero-tolerance leniency and exposes minors to full adult DUI punishment.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: What maximum fine, license suspension, and jail term apply for giving or selling alcohol to someone under twenty-one, intoxicated, or interdicted?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Buying for minors, visibly intoxicated people, or court-barred drinkers risks twenty-five hundred dollars, a one-year license suspension, and twelve months jailed.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: How do the consequences for an underage driver at point zero eight BAC compare with someone who supplies alcohol to a minor?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: An underage point-oh-eight driver faces adult DUI penalties, while the person handing over the alcohol risks a fine, suspension, and jail.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: What minimum fine, minimum service hours, maximum jail, and suspension span hit someone under twenty-one using a fake ID for alcohol?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Flashing a fake ID to buy or drink brings at least five hundred dollars, fifty service hours, up to twelve months jail, and six-to-twelve-month suspension.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: How do the fine and suspension bounds for supplying alcohol to a minor compare with using a fake ID under twenty-one?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Suppliers face ceilings up to twenty-five hundred dollars and one year suspended, whereas fake-ID users start at five hundred dollars, fifty hours, and six months.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: Which everyday vehicles and weight range does a regular Virginia driver's license cover?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Your standard license covers passenger cars and small trucks weighing twenty-six thousand pounds or less that don't fall under commercial rules.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: Which five heavy, passenger, school-bus, or hazardous vehicle categories require a commercial driver's license?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Stepping into tractor-trailers, passenger buses, tank vehicles, school buses seating sixteen or more, or hazardous materials requires a full CDL.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: Where is the boundary between a regular Virginia driver's license and a commercial driver's license?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Regular licenses stop at twenty-six thousand pounds outside commercial classes, whereas CDLs govern tractor-trailers, buses, tankers, sixteen-plus school buses, and hazmat.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: What exams and license stamp are required to drive a Virginia school bus carrying fifteen or fewer riders?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Even without a full CDL, fifteen-rider school-bus drivers must pass commercial and school-bus written exams for a cap-stamped endorsement.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: How does licensing for a fifteen-passenger school bus differ from a school bus carrying sixteen or more?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Adding that sixteenth rider crosses the federal commercial line—fifteen riders use a stamped endorsement while sixteen-plus demands a CDL.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: What does an International Driving Permit actually do, who issues it, who is barred, and what should foreign visitors carry?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: An IDP grants zero driving privilege on its own—AAA issues it to non-suspended holders for abroad, while foreign visitors pair home licenses with translations.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: Who is barred from getting an AAA international permit, and what should accompany a visitor's foreign home license?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Suspended or revoked drivers cannot obtain an AAA international permit, and international visitors driving in Virginia should keep an English translation alongside their valid home license.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: What legal standing do retail or online 'international driver licenses' have, and what crime is selling one?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Retail 'international licenses' never authorize driving anywhere, and selling any fake license document in Virginia is a Class 1 misdemeanor.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: How does a legitimate AAA International Driving Permit differ from a store-bought international license?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Neither replaces a real government license, yet AAA's booklet legitimately translates abroad while peddling store-bought 'licenses' commits a Class 1 misdemeanor.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Who gets the right-of-way at pedestrian crossings, and what two steps apply when entering from a private road or driveway?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Pulling out of a driveway without halting first blindsides sidewalk walkers and oncoming street cars.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: How does entering from a private driveway or road differ from yielding at a pedestrian crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Approaching a crosswalk calls for yielding to walkers, whereas leaving private property demands a complete stop first.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: When turning left after checking that your path looks open, which three opposing road users still get priority?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Cutting across oncoming lanes catches straight-through cars, cyclists, and crosswalk pedestrians off guard.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: Before completing a left turn across an intersection, whom must you let pass from the opposite direction?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Misjudging the closing speed of an oncoming cyclist or sedan causes classic intersection T-bone crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: What two mandatory actions apply before pulling onto a public street from a private road or driveway?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Rolling straight off a residential apron or lot entrance breaks right-of-way law for both cars and pedestrians.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: When two vehicles arrive together at an intersection with zero signs or signals, who yields to whom?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Giving priority to the vehicle on your right breaks ties cleanly when unsigned crossroads meet.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: Which driver must wait when two cars reach an unsigned, unsignaled intersection at the exact same moment?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Test questions swap left and right wording to see if you still grant priority to the car on the right.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: Who gets priority in marked crosswalks and unmarked intersections, and why do turns on red demand extra care?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Drivers craning left to spot a traffic gap on red often overlook pedestrians or cyclists stepping off the right curb.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: Why must drivers turning on red watch marked crosswalks and unmarked intersections so closely?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Turning against a red signal puts your front bumper straight across active pedestrian and bicycle paths.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: How must you respond when an emergency vehicle approaches from behind with lights or siren — and what rule covers funeral processions?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Clearing immediately to the right curb opens a lane for responders, while cutting through a funeral cortege is unlawful.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: What two options govern passing a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck displaying flashing lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Shifting into a nonadjacent lane gives roadside crews breathing room, and slowing carefully protects them when traffic blocks your move.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: Contrast what Virginia law requires for a moving emergency vehicle behind you versus a flashing rig parked ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Freezing in place beside a parked tow truck blocks traffic, whereas failing to stop for an approaching siren traps responders.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: At which two crossing types must Virginia drivers yield so pedestrians and bicyclists can cross safely?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Missing paint at a neighborhood street corner never erases a walker's or cyclist's legal right to cross.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Who holds legal priority when a pedestrian or bicyclist crosses at an unmarked intersection or marked crosswalk?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Assuming cars own intersections without white stripes is a classic exam mistake and a serious street hazard.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: Which four speed, yield, direction, and pedestrian steps govern entering a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Cutting across multi-lane circular traffic or forgetting crosswalk walkers at the splitter island sparks entry collisions.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: How should you manage your lane inside a roundabout, and which turn signal announces your exit?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Weaving mid-circle sideswipes neighboring drivers, while a crisp right blinker tells waiting entries you are peeling off.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: Contrast your duties when entering a roundabout against circulating through and exiting it?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Entry yields to every circulating lane, whereas drivers already inside follow signed lanes counterclockwise and signal right out.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: How long must you stay inside your chosen lane once circulating in a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Picking the signed lane before entry eliminates last-second lane cuts across curved blind spots.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: Which mirror, signal, and head-check steps must happen right before moving into another lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Glass mirrors leave side blind zones, so a quick over-the-shoulder glance right before steering prevents sideswipes.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: Walk through the exact check-and-signal sequence before steering into an adjacent lane?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Signaling before your final shoulder glance gives nearby drivers a heads-up while you verify your blind spot.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: What visual cue in your interior rearview mirror confirms it is safe to merge back right after passing?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Pulling back before the overtaken car's headlights fill your center mirror risks clipping their front corner.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: At which four road features is passing unlawful — and what multi-lane setup creates an exception?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Blind crests, bends, crossroads, and tracks hide oncoming traffic unless at least two lanes run your way.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: Alongside the mirror return rule and four no-pass zones, when is passing a stopped school bus barred — including private roads?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Only a physical barrier or unpaved median lets opposing traffic pass a loading school bus, and private roads count too.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: What passing rule applies whenever a solid line sits immediately to the left of your travel lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Crossing a solid line on your side puts you head-on into hidden oncoming traffic where sight distance is short.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: Besides avoiding single-lane hills, curves, intersections, and rail crossings, where must an overtake already be finished?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Stretching a pass across the start of a No Passing zone traps you in the opposing lane with vanishing sightlines.
